docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
The Unified Integration Layer defines how Freedomlink1 functions as a single sovereign institution across:

  • Protocol (code, deployments, infrastructure)
  • Governance (lineage, seals, signatures, doctrines)
  • Hardware (Rootstone-I)
  • Institutional layer (PPTF)
  • Multi-chain deployments
  • Epoch advancement and continuity

It lives in the freedomlink1-unified repository and is authoritative for cross-repo bindings.

docs.title: 2.1 Protocol Layer
docs.text:
Repo: freedomlink1-protocol

Scope:

  • contracts/ - Solidity and protocol logic
  • interfaces/ - external and internal interfaces
  • deploy/ - deployment scripts and tooling
  • ci/ - CI/CD pipelines
  • docs/ - protocol documentation
  • dashboard/ - UI for protocol state
  • analytics/ - metrics, leaderboard, Dune layouts
  • manifest/ - network and multi-chain manifests
  • ceremony/ - deployment ceremony scripts

The Protocol Layer is deterministic, technical, and chain-facing.

docs.title: 2.2 Governance Layer
docs.text:
Repo: freedomlink1-governance

Scope:

  • lineage/ - epoch lineage, anchors, seals, ledger
  • lineage/seals/ - sealed epoch artifacts
  • lineage/anchors/ - anchor points for hardware and epochs
  • lineage/ledger/ - epoch-by-epoch governance records
  • docs/governance/ - doctrines, proclamations, rights & duties
  • sentinel/ - sentinel directives and oversight logic
  • continuity/ - continuity and succession frameworks

The Governance Layer is sovereign, institutional, and human-facing.

docs.title: 2.3 Unified Layer
docs.text:
Repo: freedomlink1-unified

Scope:

  • unified/freedomlink1.unified.yaml - canonical unified manifest
  • unified/protocol.map.json - protocol repo mapping
  • unified/governance.map.json - governance repo mapping
  • unified/epoch.bindings.json - epoch <-> protocol <-> governance bindings
  • unified/sovereign.bindings.json - sovereign keys and signatures bindings
  • unified/deployment.bindings.json - deployment manifests and ceremonies
  • unified/rootstone.bindings.json - Rootstone-I hardware bindings
  • unified/pptf.bindings.json - PPTF institutional bindings
  • unified/multi_chain.map.json - multi-chain deployment mapping
  • versioning/*.version - version tracking for unified, protocol, governance, lineage

The Unified Layer is declarative, integrative, and system-facing.

docs.title: 3.1 Epoch Binding Model
docs.text:
File: unified/epoch.bindings.json

Each epoch entry binds:

  • a governance artifact (seal, anchor, ledger)
  • a protocol state (contracts, deployment scripts, manifests)
  • a lineage state (epoch number, merkle root, anchor)

Example:

{
  "epoch_4": {
    "merkle_root": "...",
    "seal": "freedomlink1-governance/lineage/seals/epoch_4_seal.json",
    "contracts": "freedomlink1-protocol/contracts/",
    "deployment_scripts": "freedomlink1-protocol/deploy/"
  }
}

This ensures every epoch has a verifiable technical and governance footprint.

docs.title: 3.2 Sovereign Binding Model
docs.text:
File: unified/sovereign.bindings.json

Defines:

  • founder key location
  • epoch-specific signatures
  • linkage to Rootstone-I and PPTF identity bindings

Example:

{
  "sovereign": {
    "founder_key": "/c/Users/crazy/founder.key",
    "epoch_signatures": {
      "epoch_3": "founder_epoch3.sig",
      "epoch_4": "founder_epoch4.sig"
    },
    "rootstone_identity": "rootstone.bindings.json",
    "pptf_identity": "pptf.bindings.json"
  }
}

This model ties human sovereignty to technical and hardware identity.

docs.title: 3.3 Deployment Binding Model
docs.text:
File: unified/deployment.bindings.json

Defines:

  • network manifests (mainnet, testnet, local)
  • deployment ceremony script

Example:

{
  "deployment": {
    "networks": {
      "mainnet": "freedomlink1-protocol/manifest/mainnet.json",
      "testnet": "freedomlink1-protocol/manifest/testnet.json",
      "local": "freedomlink1-protocol/manifest/local.json"
    },
    "ceremony": "freedomlink1-protocol/ceremony/deployment_ceremony.md"
  }
}

This ensures deployments are both technically valid and ceremonially recorded.

docs.title: 3.4 Hardware Binding Model (Rootstone-I)
docs.text:
File: unified/rootstone.bindings.json

Defines:

  • hardware root identity
  • governance anchor
  • protocol binding path

Example:

{
  "rootstone": {
    "hardware_root": "Rootstone-I",
    "identity_anchor": "freedomlink1-governance/lineage/anchors/rootstone_anchor.json",
    "protocol_binding": "freedomlink1-protocol/contracts/rootstone/"
  }
}

This binds physical hardware identity into the protocol and governance fabric.

docs.title: 3.5 Institutional Binding Model (PPTF)
docs.text:
File: unified/pptf.bindings.json

Defines:

  • PPTF as institutional layer
  • governance documents path
  • protocol binding path

Example:

{
  "pptf": {
    "institutional_layer": "PPTF",
    "documents": "freedomlink1-governance/docs/pptf/",
    "protocol_binding": "freedomlink1-protocol/contracts/pptf/"
  }
}

This binds institutional finance/trust structures into the protocol.

docs.title: 3.6 Multi-Chain Binding Model
docs.text:
File: unified/multi_chain.map.json

Defines:

  • supported chains
  • reference to protocol multi-chain manifest

Example:

{
  "multi_chain": {
    "chains": [
      "ethereum",
      "polygon",
      "arbitrum",
      "optimism",
      "base",
      "solana"
    ],
    "manifest": "freedomlink1-protocol/manifest/multi_chain.json"
  }
}

This keeps multi-chain expansion declarative and centralized.

docs.title: 4. Versioning and Continuity
docs.text:
Files:

  • versioning/unified.version - version of unified manifest layer
  • versioning/protocol.version - reference to protocol repo version/tag
  • versioning/governance.version - reference to governance repo version/tag
  • versioning/lineage.version - current epoch / lineage state

docs.title: 4.1 Versioning Rules
docs.text:
• Bump unified.version when bindings or manifests change in a way that affects integration.
  • Update protocol.version when the protocol repo hits a significant release or tag.
  • Update governance.version when the governance corpus or lineage hits a significant milestone.
  • Update lineage.version when a new epoch is sealed/anchored.

This creates a time-ordered, cross-repo continuity record.

docs.title: 5.1 Adding a New Epoch
docs.text:
1. Update the governance repo:
  2. add a new ledger entry
  3. add a new seal/anchor
  4. Update the protocol repo:
  5. deploy new contracts or manifests if needed
  6. Update the unified repo:
  7. add a new entry to epoch.bindings.json
  8. update lineage.version
  9. bump unified.version

docs.title: 5.2 Adding a New Chain
docs.text:
1. Update freedomlink1-protocol/manifest/multi_chain.json.
  2. Add the chain to unified/multi_chain.map.json.
  3. Bump unified.version.

docs.title: 5.3 Adding a New Hardware or Institutional Anchor
docs.text:
1. Add the anchor in the governance repo.
  2. Add the binding in rootstone.bindings.json or pptf.bindings.json.
  3. Bump unified.version.

docs.title: 6. Role of the Unified Repo
docs.text:
The Unified Repo:

  • does not execute code
  • does not store governance documents
  • does not store protocol logic

It declares how all of those pieces fit together.

It is the institutional map that ensures Freedomlink1 remains:

  • traceable
  • auditable
  • sovereign
  • extensible
  • multi-layer and multi-chain aware

over time.

docs.title: Autonomy Module Activation Spec
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 — Epoch 3: Expansion & Autonomy

This specification defines the activation conditions, governance rules, and operational safeguards for autonomous modules within Freedomlink1. It governs how autonomy engines operate during Epoch 3 and ensures sovereign continuity across lineage, identity, and hardware roots.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Autonomy modules allow Freedomlink1 to:

  • respond to governance signals
  • advance epochs
  • activate modules
  • renew signatures
  • perform lineage rollback
  • maintain institutional integrity

This spec ensures all autonomous actions remain sovereign, verifiable, and drift-free.

docs.title: 1. Autonomous Sentinel Activation Engine
docs.text: Triggers sentinel activation when drift risk is high.

docs.title: 2. Autonomous Epoch Advancement Engine
docs.text: Advances the epoch when intelligence recommends it.

docs.title: 3. Autonomous Module Activation Engine
docs.text: Activates governance modules based on recommendation signals.

docs.title: 4. Autonomous Signature Renewal Engine
docs.text: Renews the sovereign signature when anomalies are detected.

docs.title: 5. Autonomous Lineage Rollback Engine
docs.text: Rolls back lineage when critical anomalies threaten integrity.

docs.title: 6. Governance Orchestrator
docs.text: Runs all autonomy engines in sequence.

docs.title: Activation Conditions
docs.text:
Autonomy modules activate only when:

  • intelligence signals exceed thresholds
  • drift risk is high
  • anomaly detection flags integrity issues
  • governance recommendations indicate required action
  • hardware identity flags permit autonomous operation

These conditions ensure autonomy is guided, not uncontrolled.

docs.title: Governance Safeguards
docs.text:
All autonomous actions must:

  • preserve sovereign identity
  • maintain lineage continuity
  • pass RSA-4096 signature verification
  • align with Rootstone-I hardware flags
  • remain canonical and drift-free
  • record events in the autonomy ledger

Autonomy is always bounded by sovereign governance.

docs.title: Verification Requirements
docs.text:
Before activation, modules must pass:

  • SHA-256 digest checks
  • manifest integrity validation
  • hardware identity verification
  • Creator Seal verification
  • Codex lineage alignment

Verification engine: verifyCreatorSeal.ts

docs.title: Activation Workflow
docs.text:
Autonomy modules follow this sequence:

  1. Run sentinel analytics
  2. Forecast drift
  3. Detect anomalies
  4. Score epoch health
  5. Generate governance recommendations
  6. Activate autonomy engines
  7. Record events in autonomy ledger

This ensures autonomy is structured and predictable.

docs.title: Autonomy Ledger
docs.text:
All autonomous actions must be recorded in:

lineage/autonomy_ledger.json

Entries include:

  • timestamp
  • module activated
  • action taken
  • verification status
  • lineage impact

This ledger provides institutional transparency.

docs.title: Sovereign Constraints
docs.text:
Autonomy modules cannot:

  • alter identity roots
  • modify hardware identity
  • bypass signature verification
  • advance epochs without recommendation
  • activate modules without governance signals
  • perform rollback without anomalies

These constraints ensure autonomy remains sovereign.

docs.title: Closing
docs.text: The Autonomy Module Activation Spec defines how Freedomlink1 operates autonomously during Epoch 3. With identity, hardware, economic, and lineage roots established, autonomy becomes the next pillar of institutional evolution.

docs.text: Version: 1.0.0 Status: Genesis Last Updated: 2026-07-02

docs.title: Codex Overview
docs.text: The Codex contains the complete technical specifications for FreedomLink1's cryptographic systems, data structures, and verification mechanisms.

docs.title: 1.1 Hashing Algorithm
docs.text:
• Primary: SHA-256
  • Purpose: All document hashing
  • Canonicalization: See scripts/canonicalization.py
  • Verification: See scripts/hashing.py

docs.title: 1.2 Digital Signatures
docs.text:
• Standard: RFC 5652 (CMS)
  • Algorithm: ECDSA or RSA-2048+
  • Verification: See scripts/signature-verification.py
  • Key Management: Device Registry

docs.title: 1.3 Timestamp Authority
docs.text:
• Standard: RFC 3161
  • Provider: Configured in artifacts
  • Verification: See VERIFY.md
  • Chain: Timestamped -> Blockchain -> Archive

docs.title: 2.1 Tree Construction
docs.text:
• Type: Binary Merkle Tree
  • Leaf Nodes: Document hashes
  • Interior Nodes: Hash(left + right)
  • Root: Blockchain anchor point

docs.title: 2.2 Proof Verification
docs.text:
• Algorithm: See scripts/merkle-tree.py
  • Proof Format: Array of sibling hashes
  • Verification Time: O(log n)

docs.title: 2.3 Tree Updates
docs.text:
• Immutable: Old trees preserved
  • New Epoch: Fresh tree created
  • Continuity: Hash chain maintained

docs.title: 3.1 Network Configuration
docs.text:
• Primary: Ethereum Mainnet
  • Secondary: Polygon
  • Archive: Arweave
  • Contract: [Address in artifacts]

docs.title: 3.2 Anchor Strategy
docs.text:
• Root Hash: Committed to contract
  • Batch: Merkle batch in 2025Q4
  • Frequency: End of epoch
  • Verification: Cross-chain validation

docs.title: 3.3 Transaction Format
docs.text:
function anchorProof(
  bytes32 merkleRoot,
  uint256 epoch,
  bytes calldata metadata
) public

docs.title: 4.1 Document Schema
docs.text:
document:
  id: unique-identifier
  hash: sha256-hash
  timestamp: iso8601
  signatures: [signatures]
  metadata: key-value

docs.title: 4.2 Governance Records
docs.text:
governance_record:
  type: amendment|ceremony|vote
  proposer: contributor-id
  date: timestamp
  content: full-text
  votes: [voter-list]
  result: approved|rejected

docs.title: 4.3 Artifact Format
docs.text:
{
  "hash": "sha256-hex",
  "timestamp": "iso8601",
  "merkle_root": "hex",
  "blockchain": {
    "network": "ethereum",
    "transaction": "0x..."
  }
}

docs.title: 5.1 Hash Verification
docs.text:
1. Compute hash of document
  2. Compare with recorded hash
  3. Verify timestamp
  4. Check blockchain anchor

docs.title: 5.2 Signature Verification
docs.text:
1. Extract signature from document
  2. Get signer's public key
  3. Verify signature using public key
  4. Check timestamp of signature
  5. Verify TSA timestamp

docs.title: 5.3 Tree Verification
docs.text:
1. Collect leaf hashes
  2. Reconstruct tree bottom-up
  3. Verify root matches anchor
  4. Check blockchain commitment

docs.title: 6.1 Canonicalization (canonicalization.py)
docs.text:
• Deterministic document representation
  • Consistent hash output
  • Platform-independent
  • Idempotent transformation

docs.title: 6.2 Hashing (hashing.py)
docs.text:
• SHA-256 computation
  • Batch processing
  • Canonical form enforcement
  • Output verification

docs.title: 6.3 Merkle Tree (merkle-tree.py)
docs.text:
• Tree construction
  • Root computation
  • Proof generation
  • Proof verification

docs.title: 6.4 Signature Verification (signature-verification.py)
docs.text:
• ECDSA/RSA verification
  • RFC 3161 timestamp checking
  • Key lookup in registry
  • Audit trail generation

docs.title: 6.5 Root Comparison (root-comparison.py)
docs.text:
• Compare computed vs. recorded roots
  • Identify discrepancies
  • Generate verification report
  • Highlight problematic hashes

docs.title: 7.1 Hash Mismatch
docs.text:
• Detection: Verify script output
  • Investigation: Check source document
  • Resolution: Review change history
  • Report: Create incident record

docs.title: 7.2 Signature Failure
docs.text:
• Cause: Invalid key or tampering
  • Recovery: Check timestamp
  • Investigation: Review device logs
  • Remedy: Ceremony rollback if needed

docs.title: 7.3 Blockchain Anchor Issues
docs.text:
• Problem: Transaction failed
  • Retry: Resubmit with new timestamp
  • Fallback: Use alternate network
  • Record: Document delay

docs.title: 8.1 Timing
docs.text:
• Hash computation: < 1ms per document
  • Signature verification: < 10ms
  • Merkle proof verification: < 50ms
  • Full verification: < 1 second

docs.title: 8.2 Scalability
docs.text:
• Documents: Unlimited (sharded)
  • Batch size: Up to 10,000 per epoch
  • Storage: O(n) for n documents
  • Lookup: O(log n) via tree

docs.title: 8.3 Security Assumptions
docs.text:
• SHA-256: No known preimages
  • ECDSA: 256-bit security
  • RSA-2048: 112-bit symmetric security
  • Blockchain: Immutable ledger

docs.title: Standards Compliance
docs.text:
• ✓ RFC 3161 (Timestamp Protocol)
  • ✓ RFC 5652 (CMS)
  • ✓ FIPS 186-4 (DSS)
  • ✓ EIP-191 (Signed Data)
  • ✓ EIP-712 (Structured Signing)

docs.title: ✦ Freedomlink1 Document Creation Ceremony
docs.text:
Genesis Ritual — Epoch 6

The Document Creation Ceremony defines the sovereign ritual stewards use when creating a Freedomlink1 institutional artifact. It records authority-bounded intent, lineage continuity, identity provenance, declared hardware trust, economic continuity alignment, verification boundaries, and multi-surface recording.

This ceremony applies to governance, continuity, verification, hardware trust, economic, lineage, identity, automation, and stewardship documents. It defers to applicable governance approval evidence. It does not grant authority. It does not validate runtime behavior. It does not claim chain-state correctness. It does not claim economic execution correctness. It does not perform autonomous action.

docs.title: ✦ Invocation
docs.text: By authority of the Freedomlink1 Institution, I initiate the creation of a new institutional artifact. I affirm sovereign intent and acknowledge the institutional boundaries governing this action.

docs.title: ✦ Authority Evidence Acknowledgment
docs.text: I acknowledge that authority derives solely from approval evidence. This ceremony does not grant authority. This action defers to governance approval records where applicable.

docs.title: ✦ Lineage Continuity
docs.text: I acknowledge lineage continuity and affirm alignment with Epoch 6. I recognize the declared lineage anchors and maintain continuity with prior institutional artifacts.

docs.title: ✦ Identity Provenance
docs.text: I affirm sovereign identity provenance. I declare the steward identity responsible for initiating this artifact. I acknowledge that identity metadata is declared, not attested.

docs.title: ✦ Hardware Trust
docs.text: I invoke Rootstone-I hardware trust binding. I affirm hardware trust invocation under declared hardware identity. I acknowledge declared hardware identity and physical sovereignty binding. I affirm that hardware trust is invoked, not enforced.

docs.title: ✦ Economic Continuity Alignment
docs.text: I affirm alignment with PPTF Treasury Governance. I acknowledge declared economic configuration and economic continuity boundaries. I affirm economic continuity alignment with treasury governance policy. I affirm that economic continuity defines policy, not execution.

docs.title: ✦ Verification Boundaries
docs.text: I acknowledge that verification is limited to local artifacts. This verification does not validate runtime behavior. This ceremony does not claim chain-state correctness. This ceremony does not claim economic execution correctness. I affirm that verification is steward-initiated and bounded.

docs.title: ✦ Declaration of Document Purpose
docs.text: I declare the creation of the following institutional artifact: [Insert Document Name] I affirm its scope, boundaries, and institutional alignment.

docs.title: ✦ Multi-Surface Recording
docs.text: I record this action across all required institutional surfaces: - governance surfaces - continuity surfaces - verification surfaces - identity surfaces - hardware trust surfaces - economic continuity surfaces I affirm that recording does not imply authority or verification.

docs.title: ✦ Closure
docs.text:
I close this ceremony in alignment with the Freedomlink1 Unified Layer. This artifact is prepared for entry into the institutional lineage under Epoch 6, subject to applicable approval evidence.

Freedomlink1 Unified Layer Document Creation Ceremony — Epoch 6

docs.title: Epoch System Overview
docs.text: FreedomLink1 divides time into discrete governance periods (epochs) with defined milestones, deliverables, and transitions.

docs.title: Current Epoch — Ascension Epoch (Epoch 7)
docs.text: Epoch 7, designated the Ascension Epoch, is the active sovereign epoch recorded in the canonical ledger. It follows finalized Epoch 6 and carries forward its reconstructed, Merkle-anchored governance graph.

docs.title: Why “Ascension”
docs.text: The name reflects the transition from uneven historical epoch records, through the reconstructed and Merkle-anchored Epoch 6, into an active epoch with a signed epoch-level lineage chain.

docs.title: Activation Record
docs.text:
• Epoch 7 Seal: commit 3348328
  • Epoch 7 Explorer Entry: commit 8ef7c87
  • Epoch 7 Continuity Index: commit 6396f14
  • Epoch 7 Lineage Node: commit 8364609
  • Canonical ledger activation: commit 1d4a858

docs.title: ✦ Freedomlink1 Sovereign Editorial Charter
docs.text:
Institutional Style Guide — Epoch 6

The Sovereign Editorial Charter defines the writing voice, formatting conventions, authority boundaries, verification phrasing, and institutional tone used across all Freedomlink1 documents. It ensures every artifact reflects the institution’s sovereign identity, continuity awareness, and constitutional limits.

This charter applies to all governance, continuity, verification, hardware trust, economic, lineage, identity, automation, and stewardship documents.

docs.title: ✦ 1. Sovereign Tone
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 documents must speak with institutional gravitas.

Use a tone that is:

  • declarative
  • intentional
  • continuity-aware
  • lineage-aligned
  • authority-bounded
  • verification-honest
  • hardware-trust-aware
  • economic-continuity-aligned

Avoid:

  • metaphor
  • flourish
  • emotional framing
  • conversational looseness
  • speculative language

The institution speaks with clarity, not persuasion.

docs.title: ✦ 2. Canonical Institutional Phrasing
docs.text:
Use these sovereign phrases consistently:

  • “By authority of the Freedomlink1 Institution…”
  • “I affirm sovereign identity provenance…”
  • “I invoke Rootstone-I hardware trust binding…”
  • “I acknowledge lineage continuity…”
  • “I affirm alignment with PPTF Treasury Governance…”
  • “I acknowledge that verification is limited to local artifacts…”
  • “I declare the following action…”
  • “I record this action across all required institutional surfaces…”
  • “This ceremony does not grant authority.”
  • “This verification does not validate runtime behavior.”

These phrases define the institution’s sovereign voice.

docs.title: ✦ 3. Structural Ritual
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 documents follow a sovereign structure:

  1. Invocation
  2. Authority Evidence Acknowledgment
  3. Lineage Continuity
  4. Identity Provenance
  5. Hardware Trust Invocation
  6. Economic Continuity Alignment
  7. Verification Boundaries
  8. Declaration of Action or Purpose
  9. Multi-Surface Recording
  10. Closure

This structure ensures institutional coherence across all layers.

docs.title: ✦ 4. Authority-Safe Language
docs.text:
Never imply authority where none exists.

Avoid verbs implying:

  • enforcement
  • attestation
  • validation
  • runtime correctness
  • autonomous action
  • implicit authorization

Use verbs that preserve constitutional boundaries:

  • affirm
  • acknowledge
  • declare
  • invoke
  • record
  • prepare
  • reflect
  • document
  • align
  • maintain

Authority is always tied to approval evidence, never ceremony or metadata.

docs.title: ✦ 5. Verification-Safe Language
docs.text:
Verification must always be described within its documented limits.

Use:

  • “verifies local artifacts only”
  • “does not validate runtime behavior”
  • “records declared configuration”
  • “updates last_check in the binding”
  • “is a steward-initiated governed write”

Never imply:

  • runtime correctness
  • chain-state correctness
  • economic execution correctness
  • hardware attestation
  • identity attestation

Verification preserves truth; it does not enforce it.

docs.title: ✦ 6. Continuity-Safe Language
docs.text:
Continuity documents must avoid implying autonomous epoch transitions.

Use:

  • “prepares an epoch transition”
  • “aligns continuity surfaces”
  • “records continuity events”
  • “acknowledges lineage anchors”

Avoid:

  • “performs an epoch transition”
  • “advances the epoch”
  • “executes continuity”

Epoch transitions require governance approval evidence.

docs.title: ✦ 7. Hardware Trust Language
docs.text:
Rootstone-I must always be described as declared, not attested.

Use:

  • “declared hardware identity”
  • “hardware trust invocation”
  • “physical sovereignty binding”

Avoid:

  • “hardware attestation”
  • “hardware verification”
  • “hardware enforcement”

Hardware trust is invoked by stewards, not enforced by systems.

docs.title: ✦ 8. Economic Continuity Language
docs.text:
Economic documents must preserve the boundary between policy and execution.

Use:

  • “declared economic configuration”
  • “economic continuity alignment”
  • “treasury governance policy”

Avoid:

  • “economic correctness”
  • “treasury execution validation”
  • “runtime economic verification”

Economic continuity defines policy, not runtime behavior.

docs.title: ✦ 9. Formatting Conventions
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 documents must follow strict formatting rules:

  • H1: Document Title
  • H2: Major Sections
  • H3: Subsections
  • Single-level bullet lists
  • No nested bullets
  • Code blocks for commands
  • Blockquotes for ceremony scripts
  • No decorative symbols except the approved section marker
  • No emojis
  • No conversational filler

Documents must be clean, sovereign, and structured.

docs.title: ✦ 10. Terminology Standards
docs.text:
Use the following terms consistently:

  • Steward — human authority
  • Institution — Freedomlink1
  • Unified Layer — documentation + verification + continuity
  • Root Build — sovereign technical base
  • Epoch — institutional time boundary
  • Continuity Surfaces — continuity documentation
  • Verification Surfaces — drift + integrity + binding
  • Hardware Trust — Rootstone-I metadata
  • Economic Continuity — PPTF Treasury Governance
  • Lineage Anchors — declared genesis + continuity events

These terms define institutional identity.

docs.title: ✦ 11. Document Boundaries
docs.text:
Every Freedomlink1 document must explicitly state:

  • what it does
  • what it does not do
  • what authority it defers to
  • what verification it cannot claim
  • what runtime behavior it cannot imply
  • what autonomous action it cannot perform

This preserves institutional legitimacy.

docs.title: ✦ 12. Sovereign Closure
docs.text:
Documents must end with:

Freedomlink1 Unified Layer [Document Name] — Epoch 6

This marks the artifact as part of the institutional lineage.

Freedomlink1 Unified Layer Freedomlink1 Sovereign Editorial Charter — Epoch 6

docs.title: ✦ Root Build Economic Continuity Charter
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 Root Build • Sovereign Economic Constitution

The Root Build Economic Continuity Charter describes the policy requirements and verification boundaries for economic continuity within the Freedomlink1 Institution. It covers declared economic rules across governance, lineage, identity, hardware, treasury, and Unified Layer concerns.

This charter records institutional requirements; it does not establish that every requirement is enforced by a contract or operational system.

docs.title: ✦ Economic Continuity Overview
docs.text:
Institution: Freedomlink1 Configured Epoch: 6 — Continuity Epoch Declared Economic Authority: PPTF Treasury Governance Root Build Role: Economic and integration definitions Verification Surfaces: Drift Detector, Unified Layer Integrity Report Continuity Surfaces: Continuity Report, Epoch Advancement Document

Economic continuity is the governed preservation of economic policy, approvals, and records across time. The binding declares PPTF alignment, governance-controlled minting, and a non-inflationary supply policy unless authorized. Those declarations are not, by themselves, proof of treasury execution or full on-chain enforcement.

docs.title: ✦ 1. Economic Sovereignty Principles
docs.text: The following are policy requirements for economic actions:

docs.title: 1. Governance Primacy
docs.text: Economic actions require authorization through the applicable governance process. For FL1-C minting, the contract checks whether the configured GovernanceRouter authorizes the caller; this does not prove that broader treasury approval requirements are enforced by the token contract.

docs.title: 2. Lineage Anchoring
docs.text: Economic events should be recorded in the applicable authoritative lineage system before being described as lineage-anchored. The FL1-C genesis event is distinct from later treasury or token events.

docs.title: 3. Identity Provenance
docs.text: Stewards must establish the identity and authority of participants under the applicable policy. Creator binding at deployment does not attest every later minter, recipient, or treasury actor.

docs.title: 4. Hardware Trust
docs.text: Rootstone-I metadata may support institutional trust requirements. A declared binding does not attest each later economic action or establish live hardware state.

docs.title: 5. Treasury Alignment
docs.text: Economic actions must follow applicable PPTF policy, approvals, and records. A binding flag is not evidence that the treasury executed or approved an action.

docs.title: 6. Unified Layer Evidence
docs.text: Local drift and integrity artifacts may support review of declared metadata. They do not establish runtime, deployment, treasury, or external-state correctness.

docs.title: ✦ 2. Economic Continuity Components
docs.text: Economic continuity review considers:

docs.title: Governance Layer
docs.text: Authorization and approval records under the applicable governance process.

docs.title: Lineage Layer
docs.text: Authoritative records of approved economic events and relevant epoch transitions.

docs.title: Identity Layer
docs.text: Evidence that responsible actors satisfy applicable identity and authorization requirements.

docs.title: Hardware Layer
docs.text: Rootstone-I metadata or separately collected hardware evidence when required by policy.

docs.title: Treasury Layer
docs.text: PPTF policy, approval, custody, execution, and reporting records, as applicable.

docs.title: Unified Layer
docs.text:
Declared bindings and scoped local reports that support documentation review without substituting for the underlying evidence.

These components form a policy and evidence model; their inclusion here does not prove that they are integrated or enforced end to end.

docs.title: ✦ 3. Root Build Economic Role
docs.text:
The Root Build provides or references:

  • declared economic integration rules
  • treasury governance documentation
  • binding metadata for FL1-C
  • lineage and continuity references
  • local verification tooling and reports

The Root Build documentation and local drift detector do not execute PPTF treasury policy. The FL1-C treasury integration document describes the implementation boundary: the token checks GovernanceRouter authorization for minting, but does not itself implement a treasury interface, supply cap, treasury allocation check, epoch enforcement, or per-action identity and hardware validation.

See the FL1-C Treasury Integration Rules for the detailed policy and contract boundary.

docs.title: ✦ 4. Economic Continuity Rules
docs.text: The following are policy requirements. Their satisfaction must be supported by relevant governance and operational evidence; a local metadata match alone is insufficient.

docs.title: 1. Declared Treasury Policy
docs.text: Economic actions must be consistent with the applicable PPTF rules and approvals. See Treasury Governance.

docs.title: 2. Governance Authorization
docs.text: Required actors and approvals must be established under the governing process. For FL1-C minting, the contract-level check is limited to GovernanceRouter authorization of the caller.

docs.title: 3. Lineage Continuity
docs.text: Record economic events in the authoritative lineage system where required. Do not describe an action as lineage-recorded based only on a genesis anchor or declared path.

docs.title: 4. Identity Provenance
docs.text: Verify the identity and authority of actors as required for the specific action; creator provenance alone does not cover all later actions.

docs.title: 5. Hardware Trust Binding
docs.text: Review hardware metadata and obtain separate attestation evidence if required. A configured Rootstone-I reference is not runtime hardware verification.

docs.title: 6. Unified Layer Review
docs.text: Review the latest local report and relevant documentation, while preserving the stated verification scope and recording unresolved checks.

docs.title: Drift Detector
docs.text: The detector checks selected binding fields against a local lineage artifact and checks that the declared cross-layer consistency flags, including economic, are enabled. It does not validate the values or enforce the economic policy, and it does not inspect treasury execution or supply behavior.

docs.title: Integrity Report
docs.text: The Unified Layer Integrity Report describes declared configuration and local-check scope. It explicitly does not independently verify treasury operations or deployed behavior.

docs.title: Continuity Report
docs.text: The Unified Layer Continuity Report documents continuity declarations. It is not a transaction ledger or independent economic audit.

docs.title: Treasury Integration Rules
docs.text: The FL1-C Treasury Integration Rules distinguish declared policy from implemented contract behavior and list required evidence for a full integration claim.

docs.title: Binding Metadata
docs.text:
The binding records economic declarations and a general drift-detector last_check timestamp. That timestamp records when the detector ran; it is not a separate timestamp proving economic-policy verification.

Verification is limited to the artifacts and scope explicitly reviewed. It does not verify treasury execution, deployed contract state, actual supply behavior, runtime authorization, or deployment correctness.

docs.title: ✦ 6. Economic Continuity Constraints
docs.text:
Under applicable policy, stewards should not declare an economic action or transition fully reviewed when required evidence is missing or unresolved, including:

  • unresolved relevant drift or metadata discrepancies
  • missing required lineage records
  • missing identity or hardware evidence where required
  • absent treasury approval or execution records
  • governance authorization or signature requirements not met
  • incomplete review of relevant integrity and continuity records
  • unmet epoch-advancement requirements

The local drift detector does not enforce these constraints or prevent an economic action. Its result must not be used as a substitute for the required governance decision.

docs.title: ✦ 7. Policy Gaps and Steward Obligations
docs.text: Two existing automation behaviors require explicit stewardship:

docs.title: 1. Autonomous Epoch Wrapper
docs.text:
scripts/autonomous_epoch_advancement.py can invoke scripts/advance_epoch.py based on a matching recommendation in the intelligence ledger. The target script updates the epoch ledger and leaves the new sovereign signature as pending; it does not perform the verification or authorization checks described by the epoch protocol.

This behavior conflicts with the policy that epoch changes require governed authorization and valid records. Do not treat a recommendation or this script's output as an approved economic or epoch transition. Use the applicable governance process and review the ledger changes.

docs.title: 2. Drift Detector Binding Mutation
docs.text:
unified/scripts/drift_detector.py writes unified_layer.drift_detection.last_check into the FL1-C binding and writes a report. This is a real metadata mutation, not a read-only check. Run it only as reviewed steward work, inspect the diff, and do not interpret the timestamp as proof of economic-policy verification.

Stewards must account for these behaviors when reviewing continuity evidence; this charter does not change or disable the scripts.

docs.title: ✦ 8. Steward Responsibilities
docs.text:
Stewards should:

  • maintain economic documentation and identify policy sources
  • review drift output within its local-artifact scope
  • update integrity surfaces only with supported evidence
  • preserve authoritative lineage and signed governance records
  • review identity and hardware evidence where required
  • confirm treasury approval and execution using the applicable records
  • prepare epoch transitions under the governing protocol
  • review generated file changes before committing
  • preserve sovereign audit boundaries and unrelated workspace files

Stewardship requires accurate representation of both policy and implementation.

docs.title: ✦ 9. Economic Continuity Across Epochs
docs.text:
Economic continuity across epochs requires a governed review of:

  • required governance authorization and signatures
  • relevant lineage records and epoch alignment
  • participant identity and hardware evidence where required
  • treasury policy, approval, and execution records
  • scoped local drift and integrity results
  • applicable continuity documentation

Epoch advancement must follow the Epoch Advancement Protocol. A clean local drift result alone is not economic continuity verification and does not authorize an epoch transition.

docs.title: ✦ Closing
docs.text:
The Root Build Economic Continuity Charter defines policy expectations and evidence boundaries for economic continuity within Freedomlink1. It supports coherent stewardship across governance, lineage, identity, hardware, treasury, and Unified Layer concerns while distinguishing declarations from implemented and independently verified behavior.

Freedomlink1 Root Build Economic Continuity Charter — Epoch 6

docs.title: Sovereign Codex Page
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 — Codex Lineage Surface

The Sovereign Codex is the institutional ledger of Freedomlink1. It records the genesis of the institution, its lineage, its epochs, and its sovereign actions. This page presents the foundational lineage entries: GENESIS-0 and Codex Node #1.

docs.title: GENESIS-0 — The Origin Node
docs.text:
Node ID: GENESIS-0 Epoch: Genesis Role: Foundational Identity and Lineage Root Timestamp: 2026-09-11T00:00:00-05

GENESIS-0 establishes the sovereign identity of Freedomlink1. It anchors the Creator Seal, the hardware identity, the economic identity, and the initial governance structure.

Anchors:

  • creator-seal.json
  • rootstone-identity.json
  • pptf-identity-anchor.json

GENESIS-0 is immutable and serves as the root of all future lineage entries.

docs.title: Codex Node #1 — Expansion Epoch Initiation
docs.text:
Node ID: NODE-1 Epoch: Epoch 3 — Expansion & Autonomy Role: First Descendant Lineage Entry Timestamp: 2026-09-11T00:01:00-05

Codex Node #1 marks the beginning of institutional evolution beyond genesis. It records the activation of the Expansion Epoch, autonomy systems, and the continuation of Sovereign Genesis lineage.

Anchors:

  • GENESIS-0
  • creator-seal.json
  • rootstone-identity.json
  • pptf-identity-anchor.json
  • epoch-advancement-3.json

Codex Node #1 is fully signed, verified, and canonical.

docs.title: Lineage Continuity
docs.text:
The Sovereign Codex maintains strict lineage continuity:

  1. GENESIS-0 — Origin
  2. NODE-1 — First Expansion Node

Each node is:

  • cryptographically signed
  • timestamped
  • anchored to identity, hardware, and economic roots
  • verified through the Creator Seal

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
All Codex nodes must pass:

  • RSA-4096 signature verification
  • SHA-256 manifest integrity checks
  • lineage continuity validation
  • canonical JSON structure validation

Verification engine: verifyCreatorSeal.ts

docs.title: Purpose of the Codex
docs.text:
The Sovereign Codex preserves:

  • institutional memory
  • lineage evolution
  • governance actions
  • epoch transitions
  • sovereign identity continuity

It is the authoritative record of Freedomlink1's existence and evolution.

docs.title: Closing

docs.title: ✦ Freedomlink1 Sovereign Lint Report Format
docs.text:
CI Audit Artifact — Epoch 6

The Sovereign Lint Report Format defines the canonical structure for reporting editorial linting results across institutional surfaces. It keeps lint output authority-bounded, verification-bounded, continuity-aligned, hardware-trust-aware, and economic-continuity-aligned.

This format applies to governance, continuity, verification, hardware trust, economic, lineage, identity, automation, and stewardship artifacts. A lint report records the result of local checks. It does not grant authority. It does not establish runtime correctness. Linting does not perform autonomous action.

docs.title: ✦ Report Declaration
docs.text: By authority of the Freedomlink1 Institution, I declare the sovereign linting report for the evaluated artifacts. I affirm that this report records editorial compliance and does not grant authority.

docs.title: ✦ Authority Boundary
docs.text: I acknowledge that authority derives solely from approval evidence. This lint report does not authorize any action. This lint report does not validate any artifact. This lint report does not enforce policy. This lint report does not certify any artifact.

docs.title: ✦ Verification Boundary
docs.text:
I acknowledge that verification is limited to local artifacts. This verification does not validate runtime behavior. This report does not claim chain-state correctness. This report does not claim economic execution correctness. I affirm that this report records declared configuration and is steward-initiated.

Hardware trust invocation records declared hardware identity and physical sovereignty binding. Economic continuity alignment records declared economic configuration and treasury governance policy, not execution.

docs.title: ✦ Report Structure (Canonical)
docs.text: All lint reports must follow this structure.

docs.title: 1. Report Metadata
docs.text:
report_id: <unique-report-id>
epoch: 6
generated_at: <ISO-8601 timestamp>
initiated_by: <declared steward identity>
verification_boundary: "local artifacts only"
authority_boundary: "approval evidence required"

docs.title: 2. Evaluated Artifacts
docs.text:
Each artifact entry must include its relative path, result status, and violation count.

artifacts:
  - artifact:
      path: <relative-path>
      status: "passed" | "failed"
      rule_violations: <integer>

docs.title: 3. Violations (If Any)
docs.text:
Each violation identifies the applicable rule and source location.

violations:
  - violation:
      rule_id: <rule-identifier>
      rule_section: <section-name>
      description: <canonical-rule-description>
      location:
        file: <file-path>
        line: <line-number>

docs.title: 4. Summary Block
docs.text:
summary:
  total_artifacts: <integer>
  passed: <integer>
  failed: <integer>
  total_violations: <integer>

docs.title: 5. Recording Surfaces
docs.text:
recording:
  surfaces:
    - governance
    - continuity
    - verification
    - identity
    - hardware_trust
    - economic_continuity
  note: "Recording does not imply authority or verification."

docs.title: ✦ Canonical Example
docs.text:
report_id: lint_2026_10_12_001
epoch: 6
generated_at: 2026-10-12T11:45:00
initiated_by: declared_steward_identity
verification_boundary: "local artifacts only"
authority_boundary: "approval evidence required"

artifacts:
  - artifact:
      path: docs/style_guide_quick_reference.md
      status: passed
      rule_violations: 0

  - artifact:
      path: docs/document_creation_ceremony.md
      status: passed
      rule_violations: 0

summary:
  total_artifacts: 2
  passed: 2
  failed: 0
  total_violations: 0

recording:
  surfaces:
    - governance
    - continuity
    - verification
    - identity
    - hardware_trust
    - economic_continuity
  note: "Recording does not imply authority or verification."

docs.title: ✦ Freedomlink1 Style Guide Linting Ruleset
docs.text:
Editorial Enforcement — Epoch 6

The Style Guide Linting Ruleset defines automated checks aligned with the Sovereign Editorial Charter across all Freedomlink1 documents. These rules preserve institutional tone, authority boundaries, verification limits, continuity phrasing, formatting discipline, and sovereign closure across the Unified Layer.

This ruleset applies to all governance, continuity, verification, hardware trust, economic, lineage, identity, automation, and stewardship artifacts.

docs.title: Rule ST-01 — No Metaphor or Flourish
docs.text: Reject documents containing figurative language, metaphor, or rhetorical flourish.

docs.title: Rule ST-02 — No Emotional Framing
docs.text: Reject documents containing emotional adjectives or persuasive tone.

docs.title: Rule ST-03 — Declarative Tone Required
docs.text: Require declarative, intentional phrasing in all sections.

docs.title: Rule CP-01 — Canonical Phrases Must Match Exactly
docs.text: Verify presence of required institutional phrases when applicable.

docs.title: Rule CP-02 — Reject Non-Canonical Substitutions
docs.text: Reject documents that paraphrase sovereign phrases.

docs.title: Rule CP-03 — Ceremony Phrases Must Be Exact
docs.text:
Check for exact matches of:

  • “By authority of the Freedomlink1 Institution…”
  • “I affirm sovereign identity provenance…”
  • “I invoke Rootstone-I hardware trust binding…”
  • “I acknowledge lineage continuity…”
  • “This ceremony does not grant authority.”
  • “This verification does not validate runtime behavior.”

docs.title: Rule SR-01 — Required Section Order
docs.text:
Documents must follow the ten-step sovereign structure:

  1. Invocation
  2. Authority Evidence
  3. Lineage
  4. Identity
  5. Hardware Trust
  6. Economic Continuity
  7. Verification Boundaries
  8. Declaration
  9. Multi-Surface Recording
  10. Closure

docs.title: Rule SR-02 — Reject Missing Sections
docs.text: Reject documents missing any required structural element.

docs.title: Rule SR-03 — Reject Reordered Sections
docs.text: Reject documents that alter the sovereign sequence.

docs.title: Rule AL-01 — Reject Authority-Implying Verbs
docs.text:
Reject documents containing:

  • authorize
  • validate
  • enforce
  • attest
  • guarantee
  • certify
  • approve, unless referencing evidence

docs.title: Rule AL-02 — Require Authority-Bounded Verbs
docs.text:
Require use of:

  • affirm
  • acknowledge
  • declare
  • invoke
  • record
  • prepare
  • reflect
  • align
  • maintain

docs.title: Rule VL-01 — Verification Boundaries Must Be Stated
docs.text:
Require explicit statements that verification:

  • verifies local artifacts only
  • does not validate runtime behavior
  • updates last_check
  • is steward-initiated

docs.title: Rule VL-02 — Reject Runtime Claims
docs.text:
Reject documents implying:

  • runtime correctness
  • chain-state correctness
  • economic execution correctness
  • hardware attestation
  • identity attestation

docs.title: Rule CL-01 — Reject Autonomous Epoch Claims
docs.text:
Reject documents implying:

  • performing an epoch transition
  • advancing the epoch
  • executing continuity

docs.title: Rule CL-02 — Require Continuity-Aligned Phrasing
docs.text:
Require:

  • prepares an epoch transition
  • aligns continuity surfaces
  • records continuity events
  • acknowledges lineage anchors

docs.title: Rule HT-01 — Rootstone-I Must Be Declared, Not Attested
docs.text:
Reject:

  • hardware attestation
  • hardware verification
  • hardware enforcement

Require:

  • declared hardware identity
  • hardware trust invocation
  • physical sovereignty binding

docs.title: Rule EC-01 — Reject Runtime Economic Claims
docs.text:
Reject:

  • economic correctness
  • treasury execution validation
  • runtime economic verification

docs.title: Rule EC-02 — Require Policy-Aligned Phrasing
docs.text:
Require:

  • declared economic configuration
  • economic continuity alignment
  • treasury governance policy

docs.title: Rule FR-01 — Header Hierarchy
docs.text:
Require:

  • H1 for document title
  • H2 for major sections
  • H3 for subsections

docs.title: Rule FR-02 — Single-Level Lists Only
docs.text: Reject nested bullet lists.

docs.title: Rule FR-03 — No Emojis
docs.text: Reject any emoji characters.

docs.title: Rule FR-04 — Ceremony Scripts Must Use Blockquotes
docs.text: Require blockquote formatting for ritual text.

docs.title: Rule FR-05 — Commands Must Use Code Blocks
docs.text: Require fenced code blocks for commands.

docs.title: Rule FR-06 — Section Marker Only
docs.text: Reject the section marker when used outside section headers.

docs.title: Rule TR-01 — Required Institutional Terms
docs.text:
Require consistent use of:

  • Steward
  • Institution
  • Unified Layer
  • Root Build
  • Epoch
  • Continuity Surfaces
  • Verification Surfaces
  • Hardware Trust
  • Economic Continuity
  • Lineage Anchors

docs.title: Rule TR-02 — Reject Undefined Terms
docs.text: Reject documents introducing new institutional terms without definition.

docs.title: Rule DB-01 — Boundary Declaration Required
docs.text:
Documents must explicitly state:

  • what they do
  • what they do not do
  • what authority they defer to
  • what verification they cannot claim
  • what runtime behavior they cannot imply
  • what autonomous action they cannot perform

Reject documents lacking boundary declarations.

docs.title: Rule SC-01 — Required Closing Block
docs.text:
Require the institutional footer format:

Freedomlink1 Unified Layer [Document Name] — Epoch N

The footer epoch is selected as follows:

  1. Use an explicit epoch declared in document metadata, the title, or the filename when present. This preserves historical Epoch 6 closures after the canonical ledger advances.
  2. Otherwise, use the active epoch recorded in lineage/epoch-ledger.md.
  3. For an unmarked historical document that already has a valid earlier-epoch footer, preserve that footer instead of rewriting it to the active epoch.

Epoch identifiers 1 through 7 are recognized. New Epoch 7 documents must declare Epoch 7 and close with an Epoch 7 footer. Historical Epoch 1–6 documents retain their declared epoch footer.

docs.title: Rule SC-02 — Reject Missing or Altered Closure
docs.text: Reject documents without the required institutional closing block or with a footer epoch that does not match the document's declared or applicable active epoch.

docs.title: ✦ Closing
docs.text:
The Style Guide Linting Ruleset applies the Sovereign Editorial Charter and preserves Freedomlink1’s institutional voice, authority boundaries, verification limits, continuity alignment, and sovereign identity.

Write with:

  • hardware trust awareness

Avoid:

docs.title: ✦ Canonical Phrasing (Use When Applicable)

Required institutional phrases:

  • “I affirm sovereign identity provenance…”
  • “I invoke Rootstone-I hardware trust binding…”
  • “I acknowledge lineage continuity…”
  • “I affirm alignment with PPTF Treasury Governance…”
  • “I acknowledge that verification is limited to local artifacts…”
  • “I declare the following action…”
  • “I record this action across all required institutional surfaces…”
  • “This ceremony does not grant authority.”

docs.title: ✦ Structural Ritual (Document Layout)

Use:

Every document must state:

Freedomlink1 Unified Layer [Document Name] — Epoch 6

docs.title: ✦ Unified Layer Auditor's Handbook
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 Unified Layer • External Verification Guide

The Unified Layer Auditor's Handbook describes how to interpret the institution's local configuration, steward-maintained documentation, and verification artifacts. It identifies what those materials establish and what remains outside their scope.

This handbook does not grant an auditor access or authority, restrict independent audit procedures, or replace the terms of an engagement or applicable law. Independent runtime, deployment, contract, or chain-state work requires separate scope, access, and evidence; it is not performed by the local-documentation checks described here.

docs.title: ✦ Auditor Overview
docs.text:
Institution: Freedomlink1 Configured Epoch: 6 — Continuity Epoch Guide Scope: Local artifacts and steward-maintained documentation Primary Authority Evidence: Applicable governance instrument and action-specific approval record Institutional Surfaces: Governance, continuity, verification, lineage, identity, hardware trust, economic continuity, and registries

Auditors should distinguish declared configuration, supporting documentation, authoritative records, and independently verified operational evidence.

docs.title: ✦ 1. Auditor Mandate and Scope
docs.text:
Within an agreed audit scope, an auditor may examine the relevant artifacts and records, including:

  • declared configuration and steward-maintained documentation
  • continuity and verification surfaces
  • lineage anchors and authoritative event records
  • identity and hardware metadata, with appropriate safeguards
  • economic policy declarations and treasury records made available
  • governance ceremonies and approval evidence
  • automation constraints and registries

This handbook is an interpretation guide, not an authorization to access systems or modify institutional records. Auditor access, testing methods, confidentiality, and evidence handling are set by the engagement and applicable law. Preserve originals and record any separately collected evidence without representing it as part of the local checks.

docs.title: ✦ 2. Verification Boundaries
docs.text:
The current Unified Layer verification artifacts describe local metadata and on-disk checks. They do not, by themselves, verify:

  • contract runtime behavior or deployed bytecode
  • deployment correctness or live chain state
  • external governance decisions or legal status
  • treasury execution, custody, or solvency
  • external identity systems or identity attestations
  • physical hardware identity or live hardware attestation

These are limits of the artifacts described here, not a prohibition on separate procedures an auditor may be authorized to perform. Report independent procedures and results separately, with their own scope and evidence.

docs.title: ✦ 3. Authority Evidence Requirements
docs.text: Treat authority as evidence-based, not ceremonial.

docs.title: Primary Evidence
docs.text: Review the applicable governance instrument, action-specific approval record, required signatories, and authoritative decision record. The exact evidence depends on the action and governing process.

docs.title: Corroborating Context
docs.text: Steward identity records, lineage references, hardware metadata, and continuity documents may provide context. None of these alone establishes governance approval or authority to act.

docs.title: Insufficient on Its Own
docs.text:
• a ceremony or affirmation
  • a drift-detector result
  • documentation or registry presence
  • automation output or recommendation
  • a declared GovernanceRouter or AccessControl field

The FL1-C Governance Ceremony is a review record; it does not grant authority.

docs.title: ✦ 4. Interpreting Continuity Surfaces
docs.text:
Auditors may review the Continuity Report, Epoch Advancement Document, Drift Dashboard, and Integrity Report.

Interpret these as steward-maintained descriptions of declared state, references, and scoped checks. They are not, by themselves:

  • proof of runtime or chain-state correctness
  • proof of economic execution
  • proof of hardware attestation
  • substitutes for authoritative approvals, signed lineage records, or transaction evidence

Check dates, source artifacts, status fields, and verification limitations before relying on a statement.

docs.title: ✦ 5. Interpreting Verification Surfaces
docs.text:
Relevant surfaces include the drift detector source, its machine-readable report, binding metadata, and the Integrity Report.

The detector checks selected FL1-C binding fields against a resolved local lineage artifact and evaluates declared consistency flags. It does not independently validate every layer's operational state.

When run, the detector writes last_check into the FL1-C binding and writes the drift report. Treat this as a governed file mutation: inspect the version and diff, and distinguish the timestamp from proof that every domain was verified.

docs.title: ✦ 6. Interpreting Lineage Anchors
docs.text:
Auditors may compare declared lineage events, epochs, and metadata with the local artifact resolved by the detector. The binding declares lineage/FL1C_anchor.json; the workspace's resolved artifact is freedomlink1-root/lineage/FL1C_anchor.json.

A local anchor can document a declared genesis event or marker. It does not, without separate evidence, prove runtime lineage, chain-state history, external-system continuity, or that later actions were recorded. For epoch transitions, review the authoritative ledger, signatures, and Merkle-root evidence required by the Epoch Advancement Protocol.

docs.title: ✦ 7. Interpreting Identity Metadata
docs.text:
Auditors may review declared creator and steward identity references within the agreed scope. Metadata can describe intended provenance, but does not by itself establish a person's identity, authority, external identity verification, or identity at the time of a later action.

Separate declared identity fields from independently obtained identity evidence, and handle personal or sensitive information according to the engagement and applicable law.

docs.title: ✦ 8. Interpreting Hardware Trust Metadata
docs.text:
Auditors may review the Rootstone-I identity artifact, FL1-C hardware binding fields, and lineage marker. The Rootstone-I Hardware Trust Charter describes their intended role and limits.

The local drift detector checks for required hardware binding fields and a bound marker in the lineage artifact. It does not inspect the Rootstone identity artifact, validate its signature, identify a physical device, or perform runtime attestation. Hardware metadata is not physical attestation.

docs.title: ✦ 9. Interpreting Economic Continuity Metadata
docs.text:
Auditors may review the binding's declared PPTF alignment and policy fields, the Root Build Economic Continuity Charter, and the FL1-C Treasury Integration Rules.

The drift detector checks that the economic consistency flag is enabled; it does not verify the economic policy's values, treasury approval or execution, supply behavior, custody, or economic correctness. Review transaction, approval, and treasury records separately when included in audit scope.

docs.title: ✦ 10. Interpreting Governance Rituals
docs.text:
Governance ceremonies may show that a steward recorded a review and cited evidence. They do not, by themselves:

  • grant authority or establish approval
  • execute a governance or economic action
  • prove lineage, identity, or hardware attestation
  • verify runtime behavior

Compare ceremony statements with approval records and authoritative action records. Treat unsupported or pending affirmations as such.

docs.title: ✦ 11. Interpreting Automation Constraints
docs.text:
The Sovereign Automation Specification states intended policy boundaries and identifies current implementation gaps. It is not itself an enforcement mechanism.

In particular, scripts/autonomous_epoch_advancement.py can invoke the epoch-ledger update script based on an intelligence-ledger recommendation; the target script does not perform the governing protocol's required authorization and verification sequence. The drift detector also writes last_check into the binding. Auditors should compare policy statements with tool behavior and resulting file changes rather than assume the tools enforce the policy.

docs.title: ✦ 12. Interpreting Registries
docs.text:
Auditors may review the Asset Registry and Module Registry as indexes of declared assets and modules represented in local metadata and documentation.

Registry inclusion does not establish deployment, runtime state, legal recognition, chain-state correctness, or operational verification. Follow each entry's references and evidence limitations.

docs.title: ✦ 13. Auditor Conduct
docs.text:
Auditors should:

  • respect the agreed scope, access controls, confidentiality, and applicable law
  • distinguish primary authority evidence from contextual metadata
  • preserve evidence provenance and record the source and date reviewed
  • distinguish institutional local checks from independent audit procedures
  • report limitations, gaps, and contradictory evidence plainly
  • avoid changing artifacts under review unless explicitly authorized and documented
  • preserve the distinction between policy intent and implemented behavior

Auditing is observational with respect to this handbook's institutional surfaces; independent procedures remain governed by the engagement and applicable law.

docs.title: ✦ Closing
docs.text:
The Unified Layer Auditor's Handbook explains how to interpret Freedomlink1's local institutional artifacts and their verification limits. It supports review across governance, lineage, identity, hardware trust, economic continuity, verification, continuity, automation, stewardship, and registries without treating declarations as proof of operational behavior.

docs.title: ✦ Unified Layer Sovereign Continuity Ceremony
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 Unified Layer • Epoch Transition Review

This template records steward review while preparing an epoch transition. It does not grant authority, verify runtime behavior, validate chain state, or perform the epoch transition. Complete it with evidence actually reviewed; ceremonial language is not a substitute for approval, signatures, or authoritative records.

The Epoch Advancement Protocol remains authoritative for transition preconditions, lineage records, signatures, and Merkle-root requirements.

docs.title: ✦ Ceremony Record
docs.text:
Institution: Freedomlink1 Current Configured Epoch: 6 — Continuity Epoch Proposed Transition: [current epoch] to [proposed epoch] Ceremony ID: [record identifier] Date and Time (UTC): [timestamp] Steward(s): [name or institutional identifier] Governance Approval Reference: [instrument and decision record] Transition Status: [preparation / approved / recorded / deferred]

This ceremony documents a review and its evidence references. It is not the authoritative transition record.

docs.title: ✦ 1. Ceremony Invocation
docs.text:
The steward may open by stating:

I convene this continuity review under the applicable Freedomlink1 governance process. The current epoch, proposed transition, authority reference, and review status are recorded above. This ceremony does not itself authorize or execute the transition.

docs.title: ✦ 2. Authority Evidence Review
docs.text:
Record the applicable authority and approval evidence:

Governing Instrument: [protocol or rule] Approval Record: [reference or pending] Authorized Actors / Signatories: [identities and roles as established by evidence] Approval Status: [confirmed / pending / not established]

When supported by the cited record, the steward may state:

I reviewed the identified governance approval evidence for the proposed transition. A ceremony does not grant authority, and any pending approval remains outstanding.

Do not proceed to an authoritative transition while required authorization or signature evidence is missing.

docs.title: ✦ 3. Lineage Continuity Review
docs.text:
Authoritative Epoch Record: lineage/epoch_ledger.json Relevant Anchors / Events: [paths and event identifiers] Lineage Review Result: [complete / discrepancy / pending] Merkle Root Reference and Status: [reference and verification result]

The steward may state:

I reviewed the lineage and epoch evidence identified above within its documented scope. This ceremony does not write or sign the epoch ledger, create a lineage event, or establish that the transition has been recorded.

Follow the Epoch Advancement Protocol for required lineage, module, proof-of-concept, signature, and Merkle-root checks. Do not treat a local anchor marker as proof that a proposed transition is anchored.

docs.title: ✦ 4. Identity Provenance Review
docs.text:
Identity Evidence Reference: [applicable evidence for responsible actors] Review Result: [confirmed under applicable process / pending / not assessed]

The steward may state when supported by evidence:

I recorded the identity evidence reviewed for the responsible actors and its verification scope.

FL1-C creator metadata or a ceremony affirmation does not attest the identity or authority of each steward or approver.

docs.title: ✦ 5. Hardware Trust Review
docs.text:
Declared Hardware Reference: Rootstone-I Evidence Reference: [metadata or separately collected attestation] Review Result: [metadata reviewed / attestation separately verified / pending / not assessed]

The steward may state:

I recorded the available Rootstone-I evidence and its scope. A metadata reference or invocation does not itself attest a physical device or verify runtime hardware state.

This ceremony does not invoke hardware or perform attestation.

docs.title: ✦ 6. Economic Continuity Review
docs.text:
Policy Reference: Root Build Economic Continuity Charter Treasury Policy / Approval Reference: [applicable PPTF record] Review Result: [reviewed / pending / not applicable]

The steward may state:

I reviewed the cited economic policy and transition-specific evidence within the scope recorded above. Declared policy or consistency metadata alone does not prove treasury approval, execution, or supply behavior.

docs.title: Run Drift Detection When Appropriate
docs.text:
From the repository root, and only when approved for this review:

python unified/scripts/drift_detector.py

The detector checks selected local binding and lineage metadata; it does not verify runtime, deployment, chain state, treasury operations, identity attestations, or hardware attestations.

Running the detector writes unified/reports/fl1c_drift_report.json and updates unified_layer.drift_detection.last_check in unified/bindings/fl1c_binding.json. Review the command result, report, and file diff. This binding write is a governed mutation, not a read-only verification step.

Detector Result: [exit code and report reference, or not run] Binding Diff Reviewed: [yes / no / not applicable] Integrity Report Reviewed: [yes / no] Drift Dashboard Reviewed: [yes / no] Unresolved Local Checks: [list or none identified]

The steward may state:

I acknowledge that the drift result covers only the local checks and artifacts reported. It does not establish runtime or deployment correctness, and a none_detected result is not proof that every institutional layer is verified.

docs.title: ✦ 8. Continuity Action Declaration
docs.text:
Record the proposed continuity action in specific, human-readable terms:

I record the following proposed continuity action: [describe the transition, scope, affected records, intended outcome, and status].

Examples include preparing a transition record, reviewing epoch metadata, or updating supporting continuity documentation. This declaration does not modify configuration, write lineage, or advance an epoch.

docs.title: ✦ 9. Continuity and Recordkeeping
docs.text:
Identify authoritative records and supporting documents that actually require an update:

  • Governance Approval: [authoritative decision reference]
  • Epoch Ledger / Lineage Record: [updated / unchanged / pending; reference]
  • Sovereign Signature and Merkle Root: [status and references]
  • Integrity Report: [updated / unchanged; reason]
  • Continuity Report: [updated / unchanged; reason]
  • Drift Dashboard: [updated / unchanged; reason]
  • Binding Metadata: [specific approved change / unchanged]
  • Asset or Module Registry: [updated / unchanged / not applicable]

The steward may state:

I identified the authoritative transition records and the supporting surfaces affected by this action. A listed document is not itself an authoritative record, and listing a surface does not establish that it was updated.

Update supporting surfaces only when their content is affected and evidence is available. Do not modify binding, identity, hardware, or lineage records merely to complete this ceremony. Review and approve each mutation under the applicable process.

docs.title: ✦ 10. Ceremony Closure
docs.text:
The steward may close by stating:

This continuity review is closed with its evidence, status, and outstanding items recorded above. Closure of this ceremony does not mean the transition was authorized, executed, signed, or independently verified.

docs.title: ✦ Steward Responsibilities
docs.text:
Stewards using this template should:

  • follow the Epoch Advancement Protocol and applicable governance instruments
  • cite approval and evidence rather than relying on ceremonial language
  • preserve lineage, identity, hardware, and economic verification boundaries
  • review the drift detector's binding mutation if the detector is run
  • update only continuity surfaces affected by the transition
  • avoid using the autonomous epoch wrapper as approval or authorization
  • record pending and unresolved matters without presenting them as complete
  • commit approved changes intentionally and preserve unrelated workspace files

docs.title: ✦ Closing
docs.text:
The Unified Layer Sovereign Continuity Ceremony provides a structured record for steward review while preparing an epoch transition. It supports continuity and transparency while preserving the distinction between ceremony, authority, execution, authoritative records, and independently verified evidence.
