docs.title: ✦ Unified Layer Institutional Codex
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 • Institutional Layer Codex

The Unified Layer Institutional Codex is a consolidated reference to the declared architecture, governance expectations, and verification boundaries of the Freedomlink1 Institution. It connects governance, lineage, identity, hardware trust, economic continuity, verification, continuity, automation, stewardship, registries, and temporal governance.

This codex is an index and interpretive overview, not a substitute for governing instruments, signed decisions, authoritative lineage records, or action-specific evidence. Where descriptions differ, applicable law, approved governance instruments, and authoritative records control. Inclusion in this document does not establish that a system is deployed, operational, or independently verified.

docs.title: ✦ Institutional Overview
docs.text:
Institution: Freedomlink1 Configured Epoch: 6 — Continuity Epoch Institutional Layers: Governance, lineage, identity, hardware trust, economic continuity, Unified Layer, verification, continuity, automation, stewardship, registries, and temporal governance

Institutional configuration is represented by declared metadata, steward-maintained documentation, and authoritative records. Each source must be read within its stated verification scope.

docs.title: ✦ 1. Sovereign Principles
docs.text: The following principles summarize expectations across the institutional documentation:

docs.title: 1. Steward Primacy
docs.text: Authority requires action-specific approval evidence under applicable governance instruments.

docs.title: 2. Lineage Continuity
docs.text: Required institutional events are recorded through the applicable authoritative lineage process.

docs.title: 3. Identity Provenance
docs.text: Identity claims require appropriate evidence; metadata declarations alone do not attest an actor.

docs.title: 4. Hardware Trust
docs.text: Rootstone-I is the declared hardware identity reference. Metadata does not establish physical device identity or runtime attestation.

docs.title: 5. Economic Continuity
docs.text: Economic actions follow applicable PPTF policy and approval records. Declared configuration does not prove treasury execution.

docs.title: 6. Verification Boundaries
docs.text: Verification claims are limited to the artifacts and checks actually examined.

docs.title: 7. Continuity Preservation
docs.text: Epoch transitions follow the governing protocol and preserve required records and approvals.

docs.title: 8. Documentation Integrity
docs.text: Documentation distinguishes declared configuration from verified evidence and unresolved questions.

docs.title: 9. Automation Constraints
docs.text: Automation may assist with preparation and scoped checks but is not itself governance authority.

docs.title: 10. Audit Boundaries
docs.text: No local report implies runtime enforcement, deployment correctness, or chain-state validation unless supported by separate evidence.

docs.title: ✦ 2. Governance Layer
docs.text: Governance actions are subject to applicable instruments and action-specific approval records.

docs.title: Governance Authority
docs.text: Bindings name GovernanceRouter and AccessControl, but those declarations do not establish an individual's authority or verify a particular approval.

docs.title: Governance Ceremony
docs.text: The FL1-C Governance Ceremony provides a structured review record. It does not itself grant authority, approve an action, or execute it.

docs.title: Governance Constraints
docs.text:
• ceremonies do not grant authority
  • drift checks do not grant authority
  • documentation does not grant authority
  • approval status must be supported by authoritative evidence

docs.title: ✦ 3. Lineage Layer
docs.text: Lineage artifacts support institutional continuity and temporal records.

docs.title: Lineage References
docs.text: The FL1-C binding declares lineage/FL1C_anchor.json; the resolved workspace artifact is freedomlink1-root/lineage/FL1C_anchor.json. Declared and resolved paths should not be conflated.

docs.title: Lineage Duties
docs.text: Stewards review lineage evidence and record events through the applicable authoritative process. An existing anchor does not prove later actions have been recorded.

docs.title: Lineage Constraints
docs.text: Local metadata comparisons do not verify runtime behavior or replace protocol-required lineage and Merkle-root checks.

docs.title: ✦ 4. Identity Layer
docs.text: Identity metadata describes declared identity relationships and provenance references.

docs.title: Identity Duties
docs.text: Stewards cite appropriate identity evidence for relevant actors and actions. The FL1-C creator-binding declaration does not attest each later steward, minter, or recipient.

docs.title: Identity Constraints
docs.text: Metadata presence does not perform identity attestation or establish governance authority.

docs.title: ✦ 5. Hardware Trust Layer
docs.text: Rootstone-I is the institution's declared hardware identity reference.

docs.title: Hardware Metadata
docs.text: The workspace contains artifacts/rootstone-identity.json, FL1-C binding fields, and a Rootstone marker in the local lineage artifact. Their presence does not establish a physical device's identity or condition.

docs.title: Hardware Review
docs.text: Stewards record the specific metadata or separately collected attestation evidence reviewed. Ceremonial acknowledgment does not invoke hardware or perform attestation.

docs.title: Hardware Constraints
docs.text:
• no runtime hardware attestation is performed by the local drift detector
  • metadata does not enforce contract execution
  • a hardware reference does not prove an action was device-backed

See the Rootstone-I Hardware Trust Charter.

docs.title: ✦ 6. Economic Continuity Layer
docs.text: Economic policy and treasury action are governed by the applicable PPTF instruments and action-specific evidence.

docs.title: Economic Duties
docs.text: Stewards maintain treasury alignment documentation and review relevant approvals, execution records, and continuity evidence.

docs.title: Economic Constraints
docs.text:
The FL1-C binding declares PPTF alignment and minting policy. The FL1-C Treasury Integration Rules describe the boundary between those declarations and contract behavior. The drift detector does not verify treasury execution or supply policy.

See the Root Build Economic Continuity Charter.

docs.title: ✦ 7. Unified Layer
docs.text: The Unified Layer organizes declared integration metadata and steward-maintained reference surfaces.

docs.title: Unified Layer Components
docs.text:
• asset and module registries
  • continuity and integrity documents
  • drift reports and dashboards
  • governance and integration references
  • automation and stewardship policies

The Unified Layer Explorer describes the integration model. These surfaces provide documentation and visibility; they do not independently establish operational synchronization.

docs.title: ✦ 8. Verification Layer
docs.text: Verification is scoped to the tool and evidence used.

docs.title: Drift Detector
docs.text: The local FL1-C drift detector compares selected binding metadata with an available lineage artifact, checks declared governance and identity/hardware fields, and checks whether consistency flags are enabled. It does not test every domain's operation or validate runtime, deployment, chain, treasury, identity-attestation, or hardware-attestation state.

docs.title: Binding Mutation
docs.text: When run, the detector updates last_check in the FL1-C binding and writes a machine-readable report. Review the generated diff; the timestamp is not proof of economic, hardware, or end-to-end verification.

docs.title: Integrity Report
docs.text: The Unified Layer Integrity Report is a scoped static review of declared and locally checked configuration.

docs.title: ✦ 9. Continuity Layer
docs.text: Continuity documents provide supporting descriptions of institutional evolution.

docs.title: Continuity Surfaces
docs.text:
• Continuity Report
  • Epoch Advancement Document
  • Drift Dashboard
  • Integrity Report

Update supporting surfaces when relevant evidence or records change. They are not substitutes for authoritative governance, treasury, or lineage records and are not automatically synchronized by the detector.

docs.title: ✦ 10. Automation Layer
docs.text: Automation may prepare documents, registry drafts, continuity metadata, and scoped verification reports for steward review.

docs.title: Automation Constraints
docs.text:
• recommendations and metadata do not grant authority
  • local tools cannot claim runtime or chain-state verification
  • registry and continuity edits require review
  • automation must not be treated as approval to advance an epoch

Known implementation gap: scripts/autonomous_epoch_advancement.py can call scripts/advance_epoch.py based on a recommendation. The target script mutates the epoch ledger without performing the governing protocol's authorization and verification sequence. The Sovereign Automation Specification documents this gap; do not treat the wrapper as compliant or as evidence of approved advancement.

docs.title: ✦ 11. Stewardship Layer
docs.text: Stewards maintain institutional records within responsibilities established by applicable governance instruments.

docs.title: Steward Duties
docs.text:
• maintain accurate documentation and navigation
  • review local verification results and side effects
  • preserve lineage and continuity records
  • use governance ceremonies when required by process
  • maintain registries when approved and evidence is available
  • keep hardware, identity, and economic claims within their evidence scope

The Stewardship Charter describes these responsibilities. This codex does not appoint stewards or confer authority.

docs.title: ✦ 12. Registry Layer
docs.text: Registries index declared institutional assets and modules.

docs.title: Asset Registry
docs.text: The Unified Layer Asset Registry records assets represented in local metadata and documentation. Inclusion is not proof of legal recognition or deployed operation.

docs.title: Module Registry
docs.text:
The Unified Layer Module Registry records modules and their declared roles, with local verification limits.

Registry edits should identify supporting evidence and distinguish metadata declarations from operational status.

docs.title: ✦ 13. Temporal Governance Layer
docs.text: Epochs define the institution's declared temporal structure.

docs.title: Epoch Advancement
docs.text: Advancement is governed by the Epoch Advancement Protocol, including its required checks, authoritative records, signatures, and Merkle-root requirements. The Unified Layer Epoch Advancement Document summarizes cross-layer review expectations and does not replace that protocol.

docs.title: Epoch Constraints
docs.text:
• recommendations alone do not authorize advancement
  • local drift checks do not establish complete continuity verification
  • hardware metadata or invocation alone is not hardware attestation
  • epoch-ledger changes require the applicable governance process and records

docs.title: ✦ Closing
docs.text:
The Unified Layer Institutional Codex brings together the declared architecture and governance references of Freedomlink1. It supports review across governance, lineage, identity, hardware trust, economic continuity, verification, continuity, automation, stewardship, registries, and temporal governance while preserving the authority of underlying instruments and the limits of available evidence.

Freedomlink1 Unified Layer Institutional Codex — Epoch 6

docs.title: ✦ Unified Layer Verification Codex
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 Unified Layer • Verification Doctrine

The Unified Layer Verification Codex describes the principles, responsibilities, constraints, and interpretation rules for verification across the Freedomlink1 Institution. It distinguishes local metadata checks from independent evidence and operational testing.

Verification can support institutional truth by stating what was checked and what was not. A local result does not validate runtime behavior, chain-state correctness, deployment, or economic execution, and it does not grant governance authority.

docs.title: ✦ Verification Overview
docs.text:
Institution: Freedomlink1 Configured Epoch: 6 — Continuity Epoch Verification Surfaces: Drift Detector, Integrity Report, FL1-C binding metadata Continuity Surfaces: Continuity Report, Epoch Advancement Document Authority Evidence: Applicable governance instrument and action-specific approval records Local Detector Scope: Selected metadata and on-disk lineage artifact checks

Verification should be intentional, steward-reviewed, and limited to the evidence and method actually used. Other audit or technical procedures may have broader scopes when separately authorized and documented.

docs.title: ✦ 1. Verification Principles
docs.text: Verification under this local Unified Layer doctrine follows eight principles:

docs.title: 1. Evidence-Specific Claims
docs.text: Describe the artifacts, versions, and checks examined. Do not generalize a narrow result to untested systems.

docs.title: 2. No Unsupported Runtime Claims
docs.text: Local documentation and metadata checks do not validate contract behavior, deployment correctness, or chain state.

docs.title: 3. No Authority Claims
docs.text: Verification does not grant governance authority or establish action approval.

docs.title: 4. Steward Review
docs.text: Local checks are initiated and reviewed under the applicable process. Automation may execute a bounded check when explicitly requested; it must not operate as autonomous authority.

docs.title: 5. Continuity Support
docs.text: Verification may inform continuity review but does not perform or authorize a transition.

docs.title: 6. Hardware Trust Boundaries
docs.text: Hardware metadata is a declaration, not physical or runtime attestation.

docs.title: 7. Economic Boundaries
docs.text: Economic metadata describes declared policy; it does not establish treasury execution or economic correctness.

docs.title: 8. Transparent Limitations
docs.text: Report failed, unknown, and untested conditions alongside passing local checks.

docs.title: Drift Detector
docs.text:
The local FL1-C detector compares selected binding and lineage fields, checks required governance, identity, and hardware metadata, and tests whether declared cross-layer consistency flags are enabled.

When run, it updates last_check in unified/bindings/fl1c_binding.json and writes unified/reports/fl1c_drift_report.json. This is a file mutation; review the command result and diff. The detector does not inspect deployed systems, validate hardware identity artifacts, or execute economic policy.

docs.title: Integrity Report
docs.text: The Integrity Report documents declared configuration, local checks, and their limitations. It is steward-maintained documentation, not an enforcement mechanism.

docs.title: Binding Metadata
docs.text:
Binding metadata records declared configuration and the detector's last_check timestamp. That timestamp records when the detector ran; it does not establish that every field or institutional layer was independently verified.

These surfaces preserve an auditable account of local declarations and checks, not runtime correctness.

docs.title: ✦ 3. Verification Responsibilities
docs.text:
Stewards should:

  • run the local detector intentionally when appropriate
  • review its result and generated binding mutation
  • update integrity documentation only when supported by evidence
  • describe the actual verification scope
  • preserve audit boundaries and source references
  • avoid autonomous or scheduled checks being treated as governance approval
  • report unknown and untested areas without implying they passed

Verification is a steward-reviewed activity; the tools themselves do not provide steward authority.

docs.title: ✦ 4. Verification Constraints
docs.text: The local detector and the surfaces described here have these limits:

docs.title: 1. Local-Artifact Scope
docs.text: They inspect selected repository artifacts and metadata, not every institutional artifact or external source.

docs.title: 2. No Runtime Verification
docs.text: They do not inspect deployed system behavior.

docs.title: 3. No Chain-State Verification
docs.text: They do not query or validate blockchain state.

docs.title: 4. No Hardware Attestation
docs.text: They do not attest physical hardware or live device state.

docs.title: 5. No Economic Execution Claims
docs.text: They do not verify treasury approval or execution, supply behavior, or runtime economics.

docs.title: 6. No Autonomous Authority
docs.text: An automated check may run only within its approved invocation and scope; a result alone is not an institutional decision.

docs.title: 7. No Authority Inference
docs.text: Verification does not appoint a steward, establish authorization, or substitute for approval evidence.

docs.title: ✦ 5. Verification Interaction with Governance
docs.text:
Verification may support governance by providing scoped local observations and documentation for steward review.

It does not:

  • grant authority or approve an action
  • validate governance execution or contract behavior
  • establish that a named actor is authorized
  • validate chain-state governance

Governance authority depends on the applicable instrument and action-specific approval evidence. A successful local check is not approval.

docs.title: ✦ 6. Verification Interaction with Lineage
docs.text:
The detector compares selected declared lineage event and epoch fields with a resolved local anchor. This can identify specific metadata mismatches in the checked artifacts.

It does not:

  • validate runtime or chain-state lineage
  • establish continuity in external lineage systems
  • prove that later events were recorded
  • replace protocol-required lineage, signature, or Merkle-root checks

Lineage records define institutional history within their stated authority and evidence scope; a local anchor is not runtime history.

docs.title: ✦ 7. Verification Interaction with Identity
docs.text:
The detector checks required identity binding fields and a creator-bound marker in the local anchor.

It does not:

  • perform identity attestation
  • validate external identity systems
  • establish each actor's identity or authority
  • validate runtime identity behavior

Identity metadata describes declared provenance, not external identity verification.

docs.title: ✦ 8. Verification Interaction with Hardware Trust
docs.text:
The detector checks that hardware binding fields are present and that the resolved lineage anchor contains the expected bound marker.

It does not:

  • inspect or validate the Rootstone-I identity artifact's signature
  • identify or communicate with a physical device
  • perform hardware attestation
  • validate runtime hardware behavior

Hardware verification claims must distinguish local metadata review from physical or runtime attestation.

docs.title: ✦ 9. Verification Interaction with Economic Continuity
docs.text:
The detector checks that the declared economic consistency flag is enabled as part of the cross-layer flags.

It does not:

  • validate the economic policy values
  • verify treasury approval or execution
  • verify supply behavior or chain-state economics
  • prove economic continuity across epochs

Economic metadata describes declared configuration and policy, not runtime economics.

docs.title: ✦ 10. Verification Interaction with Automation
docs.text:
Automation may run a scoped local check when explicitly initiated and reviewed by a steward. It may produce reports and documented side effects; those outputs must be examined before they are relied upon.

Automation must not be treated as:

  • autonomous governance approval
  • authority to resolve drift by silently changing declarations
  • permission to modify registries or authoritative records
  • authorization to advance epochs

Known implementation gap: the repository's autonomous epoch wrapper can invoke an epoch-ledger update script based on a recommendation, without performing the governing protocol's authorization and verification sequence. The drift detector also writes last_check to the binding. These behaviors are documented policy gaps, not evidence that the automation constraints are technically enforced.

docs.title: ✦ 11. Verification Interaction with Registries
docs.text:
Verification can compare registry entries with the local references and evidence explicitly checked.

It does not:

  • validate live or deployed registry state
  • validate external registry systems
  • establish legal recognition or operational status
  • prove chain-state correctness

Registries index declared institutional structure; inclusion is not operational verification.

docs.title: ✦ 12. Verification Interaction with Epoch Transitions
docs.text:
Local results may inform preparation and review of an epoch transition, alongside the evidence required by the Epoch Advancement Protocol.

Verification does not:

  • perform or authorize epoch transitions
  • establish completion of protocol preconditions by itself
  • validate runtime epoch behavior
  • substitute for approval, signatures, lineage records, or Merkle-root evidence

The local drift detector does not block a transition or enforce a freshness threshold for its timestamp.

docs.title: ✦ 13. Verification Conduct
docs.text:
Stewards and reviewers should:

  • act intentionally and transparently
  • state which artifacts and versions were examined
  • preserve approval and authority evidence requirements
  • maintain continuity and lineage boundaries
  • distinguish hardware metadata from attestation
  • distinguish identity declarations from identity evidence
  • distinguish economic policy declarations from execution
  • disclose automation side effects and limitations
  • preserve source artifacts and report contradictory or unresolved results

Verification is disciplined evidence handling, not a claim broader than the work performed.

docs.title: ✦ Closing
docs.text:
The Unified Layer Verification Codex describes the local verification doctrine of the Freedomlink1 Institution. It supports review across governance, lineage, identity, hardware trust, economic continuity, automation, registries, and epoch transitions while preserving the distinction between local metadata checks and independently verified operational behavior.

docs.title: Epochs, Cycles, Consecration, and Seal Logic
Overview
docs.text:
The Ceremony Engine is the procedural and logical core of Freedomlink1 governance. It coordinates epoch and cycle progression, manages ceremonial state, and triggers seal formation at defined institutional milestones.

The Ceremony Engine is responsible for: - maintaining ceremony time state - coordinating steward voting phases - evaluating seal readiness - invoking Rootstone-I seal instructions

docs.title: Epoch
docs.text: An epoch is a high-level institutional era. Each epoch contains multiple cycles and governs long-term continuity.

docs.title: Cycle
docs.text: A cycle is a governance event within an epoch. The Decade Seal Cycle is the primary cycle type used in the root build.

docs.title: Consecration
docs.text: Consecration is the formal transition of ceremony state from one epoch or cycle to the next.

docs.title: Retirement
docs.text: Retirement is the decommissioning of ceremony state or hardware elements under controlled conditions.

docs.title: Flow model
docs.text:
1. Steward initialization
  2. Vote collection
  3. Policy evaluation
  4. Task enqueue
  5. Sealed execution
  6. Decade Seal generation

Each step is governed by the Ceremony Engine and anchored to the Merkle Forest.

docs.title: Seal types
docs.text:
• SEAL.BLOCK
  • SEAL.DEVICE
  • SEAL.EPOCH
  • SEAL.CYCLE
  • SEAL.CEREMONY
  • SEAL.ATTEST

docs.title: Seal process
docs.text:
• Assemble preimage from ceremony state, lineage roots, steward votes, and epoch/cycle metadata
  • Load preimage into Rootstone-I
  • Execute seal instruction
  • Hash and sign the output
  • Store the resulting seal artifact in the Merkle Forest

docs.title: Ceremony time state
docs.text:
The Ceremony Engine maintains: - ceremony_epoch - ceremony_cycle - ceremony_status - seal_ready - attestation_ready

Time state is updated only under ceremony rules and cannot be rewound.

docs.title: Governance alignment
docs.text:
The Ceremony Engine is the execution layer for: - Root build lifecycle events - Decade Seal Cycle progression - Steward role enforcement - Canonical artifact creation - Hardware-level ceremony integration

The engine is designed so that governance actions are always accompanied by a sealed, auditable artifact.

docs.title: Sovereign Board, Device Identity, and Lineage Integration
Overview
docs.text:
The Device System Architecture Codex defines how hardware, firmware, protocol, and governance align within Freedomlink1.

This codex describes: - the Sovereign Board architecture - Rootstone-I integration - lineage partitioning - identity and attestation flows - security and boot state

docs.title: Sovereign Board
docs.text: The Sovereign Board hosts: - Rootstone-I processor - secure enclave vaults - ceremony sensors - lineage storage partitions - communication buses (SBUS, IBUS, LBUS, Sensor Bus)

docs.title: Device identity
docs.text:
Device identity is derived from: - Stone identity - Device identity - certificate hashes - firmware lineage

Identity is anchored in Rootstone-I and recorded in the Merkle Forest.

docs.title: Lineage partition
docs.text:
The lineage partition stores: - root hashes - ceremony artifacts - device lifecycle records - firmware lineage proofs

This partition is immutable and only updated via sealed ceremony events.

docs.title: Secure boot
docs.text:
• Rootstone-I enforces secure boot
  • Boot state is recorded in CSR_BOOT_STATE
  • Firmware lineage is verified before execution

docs.title: Tamper detection
docs.text:
• Sensor Bus monitors environmental and physical state
  • Tamper events update CSR_TAMPER_STATE
  • Tamper lock can trigger ceremony health state changes

docs.title: Enclave integrity
docs.text:
• CSR_ENCLAVE_STATE enforces enclave policy
  • Private keys and seals are protected inside EV0
  • No debug or DMA access to enclave secrets

docs.title: Protocol alignment
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 protocol documents reference the device architecture for: - root artifact creation - ceremony engine triggers - attestation bundles - hardware-backed lineage

docs.title: Sovereign Processor, Ceremony Engine, and Lineage Root
Overview
docs.text:
Rootstone-I is the canonical sovereign processor for Freedomlink1. It is the hardware root of trust for ceremony, seal formation, attestation, and lineage enforcement.

Rootstone-I is defined by: - a ceremony-aligned microarchitecture - immutable fuse and enclave subsystems - a CSR register map for identity, seal, epoch, cycle, and security state - a bus architecture that prioritizes seal operations and lineage integrity

docs.title: SC0 — Sovereign Core
docs.text:
• Pipeline stages: FETCH → DECODE → PREIMAGE → ENCLAVE CALL → SIGN → WRITEBACK
  • Executes seal, attestation, identity, ceremony, CSR, and fuse instructions

docs.title: SE0 — Seal Engine
docs.text:
• Executes SEAL.BLOCK, SEAL.DEVICE, SEAL.EPOCH, SEAL.CYCLE, SEAL.CEREMONY, SEAL.ATTEST
  • Handles preimage load, SHA-256 hashing, signature generation, seal formatting, and counter increment

docs.title: AE0 — Attestation Engine
docs.text:
• Constructs identity and state bundles
  • Hashes and signs attestation artifacts
  • Outputs canonical attestation bundles

docs.title: EV0 — Enclave Vault
docs.text:
• Stores private keys, identity keys, seal counters, ceremony state, firmware lineage, and mask lineage
  • No external read/write, no DMA, no debug, no bypass

docs.title: CSR0 — CSR Controller
docs.text: • Manages sovereign registers for identity, seals, attestation, epoch/cycle, and security

docs.title: FM0 — Fuse Matrix
docs.text:
• Enforces irreversible security invariants:
  • identity lock
  • firmware lock
  • mask lock
  • seal counter lock
  • debug disable
  • tamper lock
  • consecration
  • retirement

docs.title: IE0 — Identity Engine
docs.text: • Manages Stone identity, Device identity, certificate hashes, and lineage anchors

docs.title: CT0 — Ceremony Time Engine
docs.text:
• Maintains CSR_EPOCH, CSR_CYCLE, and ceremony time state
  • Updates on SEAL.EPOCH and SEAL.CYCLE

docs.title: BI0 — Bus Interface Engine
docs.text:
• Arbitrates SBUS, IBUS, LBUS, Sensor Bus
  • Prioritizes ceremony-aligned operations and seal state propagation

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
• CSR_IDENTITY — Stone identity hash
  • CSR_DEVICE_ID — Device identity hash
  • CSR_CERT_HASH — certificate hash
  • CSR_FIRMWARE_HASH — firmware lineage hash

docs.title: Seals
docs.text:
• CSR_SEAL_COUNTER — monotonic seal counter
  • CSR_SEAL_PREIMAGE — preimage buffer
  • CSR_SEAL_OUTPUT — seal output buffer
  • CSR_SEAL_TYPE — seal type selector

docs.title: Attestation
docs.text:
• CSR_ATTEST_TRIGGER — trigger attestation
  • CSR_ATTEST_STATE — attestation state
  • CSR_ATTEST_OUTPUT — attestation bundle

docs.title: Epoch / Cycle
docs.text:
• CSR_EPOCH — current epoch
  • CSR_CYCLE — current cycle
  • CSR_TIME_STATE — ceremony time state

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• CSR_TAMPER_STATE — tamper detection
  • CSR_FUSE_STATE — fuse matrix state
  • CSR_ENCLAVE_STATE — enclave integrity
  • CSR_BOOT_STATE — secure boot status

docs.title: Fuse matrix
docs.text:
• FUSE_IDENTITY_LOCK
  • FUSE_DEVICE_ID_LOCK
  • FUSE_FW_LOCK
  • FUSE_FW_LINEAGE_LOCK
  • FUSE_MASK_LOCK
  • FUSE_MASK_LINEAGE_LOCK
  • FUSE_SEAL_COUNTER_LOCK
  • FUSE_SEAL_PRIVKEY_LOCK
  • FUSE_DEBUG_DISABLE
  • FUSE_TAMPER_LOCK
  • FUSE_ENCLAVE_LOCK
  • FUSE_CONSECRATION
  • FUSE_RETIREMENT

All fuses are blown only under ceremony control and are irreversible.

docs.title: SBUS
docs.text:
• Ceremony and seal operations
  • Highest priority bus for Rootstone-I

docs.title: IBUS
docs.text:
• Identity and attestation data
  • Secondary priority for identity flows

docs.title: LBUS
docs.text:
• Lineage and artifact transfer
  • Ensures consistent Merkle Forest state

docs.title: Sensor Bus
docs.text:
• Tamper, power, and environmental sensors
  • Monitored by the Ceremony Time Engine

docs.title: Ceremony alignment
docs.text:
Rootstone-I is the canonical hardware root of trust for: - Root Protocol Canon - Root Ledger Specification - Seal Logic & Cryptographic Canon - Ceremony Engine Specification

The hardware architecture is explicitly aligned to the institutional lineage model and the Root Build’s ceremonial structure.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Seal Logic Canon defines how Freedomlink1 produces canonical artifacts that represent institutional continuity, lineage, and ceremony.

It specifies: - cryptographic primitives - seal formats - preimage construction rules - verification processes

docs.title: Cryptographic primitives
docs.text:
• Hash function: SHA-256
  • Signature schemes: secp256k1, Ed25519, BLS12-381
  • Key containers: Rootstone-I private keys stored in EV0
  • Attestation bundles: Ed25519-signed state assertions

docs.title: Seal format
docs.text:
A canonical seal artifact includes: - seal type - seal counter - epoch/cycle metadata - lineage roots - steward vote summary - attestation digest - cryptographic signature

All seals are serialized in a deterministic format and anchored to the Merkle Forest.

docs.title: Preimage rules
docs.text:
Preimages are assembled from: - ceremony time state - artifact lineage roots - steward identities - policy evaluation results - task enqueue metadata

Preimages are loaded into Rootstone-I and consumed by the Seal Engine.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Verification consists of: 1. Recomputing the seal hash from the preimage 2. Validating the signature against the expected public key 3. Confirming the seal counter and epoch/cycle metadata 4. Checking the seal artifact against the Merkle Forest root

A verified seal is evidence of a valid ceremony event and an anchored governance decision.

docs.title: Canonical artifact types
docs.text:
• seal.artifact
  • attest.bundle
  • lineage.root
  • governance.cycle
  • device.identity

Each artifact type has a unique serialization schema and strict validation rules.

docs.title: Epoch Advancement Protocol
docs.text: Freedomlink1 — Sovereign Digital Institution Version: 1.0 Epoch: 2 (Root Build v1.2) Prepared by: Joshua W. Blaz

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
The Epoch Advancement Protocol ("Protocol") defines the formal process by which Freedomlink1 transitions from one epoch to the next. It ensures:

  • continuity of sovereign lineage
  • integrity of governance artifacts
  • correctness of Merkle root evolution
  • proper sealing of epoch boundaries
  • activation of new governance modules
  • preservation of institutional identity

Epoch advancement is a constitutional act and must follow this Protocol exactly.

docs.title: 2.1 Epoch
docs.text: A discrete governance period representing a stable state of the Institution.

docs.title: 2.2 Lineage Seal
docs.text: A cryptographic seal binding the final Merkle root of the epoch to the sovereign signature.

docs.title: 2.3 Advancement Trigger
docs.text: An authorized action that initiates epoch transition.

docs.title: 2.4 Sovereign Signature
docs.text: A cryptographic signature produced by the Founder's key, used to validate lineage.

docs.title: 2.5 Merkle Root
docs.text: A cryptographic digest representing the complete governance corpus.

docs.title: 3. Authority to Advance Epochs
docs.text: Epoch advancement may only be initiated by:

docs.title: 3.1 Founder (Ceremonial Steward)
docs.text: The Founder holds sovereign authority to advance epochs.

docs.title: 3.2 Governance Modules (with consensus)
docs.text: Modules may recommend advancement but cannot execute it without Founder authorization.

docs.title: 3.3 Sentinel Recommendation
docs.text: Sentinels may recommend advancement when drift, corruption, or major governance changes occur.

docs.title: 4. Advancement Triggers
docs.text: Epoch advancement may be triggered by:

docs.title: 4.1 Major Governance Additions
docs.text: New constitutional artifacts, charters, codices, or protocols.

docs.title: 4.2 Structural Governance Changes
docs.text: Changes to module architecture, lineage structure, or sovereign rights.

docs.title: 4.3 Hardware Trust Updates
docs.text: Changes to Rootstone-I or other hardware trust anchors.

docs.title: 4.4 Sentinel Alerts
docs.text: Critical alerts indicating drift or governance instability.

docs.title: 4.5 Founder Proclamation
docs.text: A direct sovereign proclamation by the Founder.

docs.title: 5. Advancement Sequence
docs.text: Epoch advancement follows this exact sequence:

docs.title: 5.1 Corpus Finalization
docs.text:
All governance artifacts for the current epoch must be:

  • indexed
  • hashed
  • registered
  • validated

docs.title: 5.2 Merkle Root Generation
docs.text: The governance pipeline computes the Merkle root for the finalized corpus.

docs.title: 5.3 Sovereign Signature Generation
docs.text: The Founder signs the Merkle root using the sovereign private key.

docs.title: 5.4 Lineage Seal Creation
docs.text:
A lineage seal is created containing:

  • epoch number
  • Merkle root
  • sovereign signature
  • timestamp
  • module state

docs.title: 5.5 Seal Registration
docs.text:
The lineage seal is stored in:

  • /lineage/seals/epoch_<n>.json
  • governance manifest
  • module registry

docs.title: 5.6 Epoch Increment
docs.text:
The epoch counter is incremented:

epoch = epoch + 1

docs.title: 5.7 Module Activation
docs.text: New governance modules for the next epoch are activated.

docs.title: 5.8 Sentinel Reset
docs.text: Sentinels reset their drift-detection baselines.

docs.title: 6. Lineage Seal Format
docs.text:
A lineage seal must contain:

{
  "epoch": <integer>,
  "merkle_root": "<sha256>",
  "sovereign_signature": "<signature>",
  "timestamp": "<iso8601>",
  "modules": {
    "active": [...],
    "inactive": [...]
  }
}

This seal is immutable once created.

docs.title: 7. Verification Requirements
docs.text: Before an epoch can advance:

docs.title: 7.1 Merkle Root Verification
docs.text: The computed root must match the governance corpus.

docs.title: 7.2 Signature Verification
docs.text: The sovereign signature must match the Merkle root.

docs.title: 7.3 Module Integrity Verification
docs.text: All modules must pass integrity checks.

docs.title: 7.4 Manifest Consistency
docs.text: The governance manifest must match the corpus.

docs.title: 7.5 Sentinel Clearance
docs.text: Sentinels must report no critical anomalies.

docs.title: 8. Failure Conditions
docs.text:
Epoch advancement must halt if:

  • signature verification fails
  • Merkle root mismatch occurs
  • module integrity fails
  • sentinel reports critical drift
  • lineage seal cannot be generated

These failures must be logged and escalated.

docs.title: 9. Founder Responsibilities
docs.text:
The Founder must:

  • verify corpus completeness
  • generate sovereign signature
  • authorize advancement
  • seal lineage
  • activate next-epoch modules
  • publish advancement proclamation

docs.title: 10. Sentinel Responsibilities
docs.text:
Sentinels must:

  • monitor advancement sequence
  • verify module activation
  • update drift baselines
  • confirm lineage seal integrity

docs.title: 11. Module Responsibilities
docs.text:
Modules must:

  • validate their own state
  • confirm readiness for next epoch
  • register updated configuration
  • report anomalies

docs.title: 12. Advancement Proclamation
docs.text:
Upon successful advancement, the Founder issues a proclamation containing:

  • new epoch number
  • lineage seal reference
  • governance changes summary
  • module activation summary

This proclamation becomes part of the governance corpus.

docs.title: FL1-C Treasury Integration Rules
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 Root Build - PPTF Treasury Governance Alignment

This document defines the intended economic governance requirements for Freedomlink1 Credit (FL1C) in relation to the PPTF Treasury Governance System. It distinguishes policy requirements and binding declarations from behavior currently enforced by the FL1C contract.

These rules do not, by themselves, create a treasury contract, authorize an action, or prove operational integration.

docs.title: Economic Governance Overview
docs.text:
• Treasury System: PPTF - Patent Protected Trust Fund
  • Asset Class: Sovereign Credit Token
  • Symbol: FL1C
  • Decimals: 18
  • Declared Governance Authority: GovernanceRouter
  • Configured Epoch: 6 - Continuity Epoch

The Unified Layer binding declares PPTF alignment, governance-controlled minting, and a non-inflationary supply policy unless expansion is authorized. These are declared integration rules; treasury execution must be provided by deployed and verified system components.

docs.title: Treasury Minting Rules
docs.text:
FL1C minting is intended to be governance-controlled. The current FL1C.sol contract enforces this authorization check on mint:

require(governance.isAuthorized(msg.sender), "Not authorized");

A successful authorized call increases totalSupply and the recipient balance. The contract does not implement a direct PPTF treasury authorization interface.

docs.title: Required Governance Conditions
docs.text:
Before authorizing minting for treasury purposes, the responsible governance process must establish:

  • Epoch alignment with the approved treasury action
  • Lineage continuity and a record of the action
  • Identity provenance for the responsible actor
  • Hardware trust evidence where required by institutional policy
  • Treasury authorization, allocation purpose, and amount

These are policy requirements. The current token contract checks only whether governance.isAuthorized(msg.sender) returns true; it does not itself enforce each condition above.

docs.title: Minting Implementation Status
docs.text: The contract does not impose a supply cap or per-epoch mint limit. Any account accepted by the configured governance router can call mint with an amount; therefore, the non-inflationary policy depends on governance controls and is not independently enforced as a token-level cap.

docs.title: Treasury Supply Model
docs.text:
The binding declares the supply model as "non-inflationary unless authorized." In implementation terms:

  • Minting requires the configured GovernanceRouter to authorize the caller.
  • The contract has no maximum supply, rate limit, or treasury allocation check.
  • An authorized caller can mint any amount accepted by the EVM's uint256 arithmetic.
  • Supply changes should be approved, documented, and auditable under the applicable treasury process before execution.

A fixed or capped supply must not be claimed unless an enforceable limit is added and verified.

docs.title: Epoch Awareness
docs.text: The binding configures epoch 6 as FL1C's lineage epoch and declares epoch awareness. The current contract stores an EpochManager reference, but does not call it or enforce epoch alignment during minting. Epoch checks must be performed by the governance process or added to the contract before they are represented as on-chain enforcement.

docs.title: Lineage Anchoring
docs.text:
The binding declares the FL1C genesis event and lineage anchor. The contract registers FL1C Token Genesis with its configured LineageRegistry during construction. It does not register subsequent mints or treasury events, nor does it update the local anchor file.

Treasury actions must be recorded in the applicable lineage system before they are described as lineage-anchored. The declared anchor path is lineage/FL1C_anchor.json; the available workspace artifact is freedomlink1-root/lineage/FL1C_anchor.json.

docs.title: Identity Provenance
docs.text: The contract calls the configured CreatorIdentityRegistry to bind the deployer during construction. This does not verify the identity of each later minter or treasury recipient. Treasury procedures must separately establish that participants are authorized and identity requirements are satisfied.

docs.title: Hardware Trust
docs.text: The contract calls the configured RootstoneBinding for the deployer during construction. This does not attest each later treasury action or prove a live hardware trust state. Such evidence must be checked by the relevant governance process and retained with the action record.

docs.title: Treasury Authorization Flow
docs.text:
The following is the required policy flow for a treasury action, not a claim that FL1C implements the complete sequence on-chain:

  1. GovernanceRouter receives the treasury request.
  2. The applicable access-control process verifies authority.
  3. The EpochManager or governance process verifies epoch alignment.
  4. Lineage records the approved action and its outcome.
  5. Required identity and hardware evidence is checked.
  6. PPTF Treasury Governance approves and executes the economic action.
  7. If the action mints FL1C, the configured GovernanceRouter must authorize the caller to the token contract.

The current FL1C contract directly enforces only the final token-level caller authorization among these checks.

docs.title: Treasury Event Types
docs.text:
The treasury process may classify actions as:

  • Minting: Governance-authorized supply expansion
  • Allocation: Distribution to approved institutional modules
  • Continuity: Epoch-based economic transitions
  • Adjustment: Governance-authorized supply or rule changes
  • Verification: Integrity or drift checks

The current contract emits its token Transfer event for minting. It registers the genesis event in the LineageRegistry during construction, but does not itself record the other event classes above. Do not describe those events as recorded or anchored until the relevant integrations are implemented and checked.

docs.title: Treasury Verification
docs.text:
Evidence may include:

  • Unified Layer Drift Detector output
  • Unified Layer Integrity Report
  • Current binding metadata
  • Lineage anchor and registry records
  • Identity registry evidence
  • Hardware attestation evidence
  • PPTF treasury approval and execution records

The drift detector checks local binding metadata against the available lineage artifact. It does not verify deployed contract state, live governance decisions, hardware attestations, PPTF execution, or treasury solvency. Verification statements must identify the evidence and scope used.

docs.title: Implementation Checklist
docs.text:
Before claiming full treasury integration, verify that:

  • The configured governance, epoch, lineage, identity, and hardware addresses are deployed and correct.
  • Epoch and treasury-policy checks are enforced at the appropriate authority boundary.
  • Supply limits or governance safeguards match the adopted issuance policy.
  • Mint, allocation, adjustment, and continuity actions are recorded in lineage and treasury systems.
  • Identity and hardware requirements are checked for relevant actors and actions.
  • Tests cover authorization failures, unauthorized issuance, policy boundaries, and event recording.

docs.title: Closing
docs.text:
The FL1C binding declares alignment with PPTF and governance-controlled minting. The current contract enforces GovernanceRouter authorization for minting and performs creator, hardware, and genesis-lineage calls during construction. Epoch enforcement, supply caps, per-action identity and hardware validation, and treasury execution are not implemented by the token contract itself.

This document defines the requirements and records that implementation boundary so future changes can be evaluated without confusing policy declarations with verified behavior.

docs.title: GOVERNANCE CHARTER ADDENDUM
docs.text: Freedomlink1 - Sovereign Digital Institution Version: 1.0 Effective Date: September 10, 2026 Epoch: 2 (Root Build v1.2) Prepared by: Joshua W. Blaz

docs.title: 1. Purpose of the Addendum
docs.text:
This Governance Charter Addendum ("Addendum") expands the foundational governance framework of Freedomlink1 ("Institution"). It defines additional governing authority, decision-making structures, sovereign rights, duties, amendment procedures, and lineage-anchoring rules required for epoch-based continuity.

This Addendum is a constitutional extension of the Institution's core governance charter.

docs.title: 2.1 Sovereign Authority
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 derives its authority from:

  • its sovereign governance engine
  • its hardware trust boundary (Rootstone-I)
  • its lineage-anchored documentation corpus
  • its Founder's ceremonial stewardship
  • its epoch-based continuity model

docs.title: 2.2 Founder Authority
docs.text:
The Founder retains:

  • ceremonial authority
  • constitutional amendment authority
  • epoch advancement authority
  • sentinel activation authority
  • final interpretive authority over governance primitives

docs.title: 2.3 Delegated Authority
docs.text:
Authority may be delegated to:

  • governance modules
  • sovereign sentinels
  • authorized contributors
  • institutional councils (future epochs)

Delegation must be recorded in sovereign lineage.

docs.title: 3.1 Governance Layers
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 governance consists of:

  • G-Tier: Institutional Governance
  • F-Tier: Sovereign Intelligence
  • E-Tier: Governance Modules
  • D-Tier: Legal Corpus
  • C-Tier: Operational Systems
  • B-Tier: Hardware Trust
  • A-Tier: Foundational Identity

Each tier has defined responsibilities and authority boundaries.

docs.title: 3.2 Decision-Making Model
docs.text:
Decisions are made through:

  • Founder proclamations
  • governance module consensus
  • sentinel recommendations
  • lineage-anchored amendments
  • epoch advancement ceremonies

docs.title: 3.3 Governance Modules
docs.text:
Modules may include:

  • security governance
  • lineage governance
  • compliance governance
  • funding governance
  • contributor governance

Modules operate under strict authority boundaries defined in this Addendum.

docs.title: 4. Sovereign Rights
docs.text:
The Institution possesses the following sovereign rights:

  • Right of Continuity: to maintain lineage across epochs
  • Right of Integrity: to preserve hardware trust boundaries
  • Right of Governance: to define and enforce institutional rules
  • Right of Amendment: to evolve governance through lineage-anchored updates
  • Right of Protection: to defend against drift, corruption, or unauthorized access
  • Right of Autonomy: to operate independently of external systems

These rights are inherent and perpetual.

docs.title: 5. Sovereign Duties
docs.text:
The Institution is bound by the following duties:

  • Duty of Preservation: maintain all lineage artifacts
  • Duty of Transparency: record governance changes in sovereign ledger
  • Duty of Security: enforce hardware trust boundaries
  • Duty of Continuity: ensure epoch transitions occur correctly
  • Duty of Stewardship: uphold institutional purpose and integrity
  • Duty of Accountability: maintain auditability of governance actions

These duties apply to all governance tiers.

docs.title: 6.1 Amendment Authority
docs.text:
Amendments may be initiated by:

  • Founder
  • governance modules
  • sovereign sentinels (recommendation only)

docs.title: 6.2 Amendment Requirements
docs.text:
All amendments must:

  • be documented in the sovereign ledger
  • include a hash manifest
  • include a sovereign signature
  • specify affected governance tiers
  • specify effective epoch

docs.title: 6.3 Amendment Ratification
docs.text:
An amendment is ratified when:

  • signed by the Founder
  • anchored into lineage
  • acknowledged by governance modules

Ratification is final and irreversible unless superseded by a future amendment.

docs.title: 7.1 Anchoring Requirements
docs.text:
Every governance action must include:

  • timestamp
  • sovereign signature
  • hash of affected documents
  • module identifier
  • epoch identifier

docs.title: 7.2 Immutable Anchoring
docs.text:
Once anchored:

  • governance records cannot be altered
  • amendments cannot be retroactively modified
  • lineage must remain cryptographically intact

docs.title: 7.3 Lineage Verification
docs.text:
Verification occurs through:

  • Rootstone-I hardware trust
  • sovereign signatures
  • hash manifests
  • epoch seals

docs.title: 8.1 Rootstone-I Authority
docs.text:
Rootstone-I enforces:

  • cryptographic integrity
  • module activation rules
  • sentinel authority boundaries
  • lineage verification
  • governance protection

docs.title: 8.2 Boundary Violations
docs.text:
Any attempt to bypass hardware trust boundaries triggers:

  • sentinel alert
  • governance lockdown
  • lineage freeze
  • Founder notification

docs.title: 9.1 Epoch Definition
docs.text:
An epoch is a governance period defined by:

  • lineage seal
  • module activation state
  • institutional continuity
  • sovereign signature

docs.title: 9.2 Epoch Advancement
docs.text:
Advancement requires:

  • Founder proclamation
  • lineage verification
  • sentinel readiness
  • governance module alignment

docs.title: 9.3 Epoch Records
docs.text:
Each epoch includes:

  • governance changes
  • legal corpus updates
  • module activations
  • sentinel logs
  • hardware trust events

docs.title: 10.1 Enforcement Authority
docs.text:
Enforcement is carried out by:

  • governance modules
  • sovereign sentinels
  • hardware trust layer
  • Founder authority

docs.title: 10.2 Violations
docs.text:
Violations include:

  • unauthorized governance changes
  • lineage tampering
  • hardware trust bypass
  • sentinel override attempts

Violations trigger automatic governance lockdown.

docs.title: Institutional Continuity Doctrine
docs.text: Freedomlink1 — Sovereign Digital Institution Version: 1.0 Epoch: 2 (Expansion Epoch) Prepared by: Joshua W. Blaz

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
The Institutional Continuity Doctrine ("Doctrine") establishes the principles, mechanisms, and safeguards that ensure Freedomlink1 persists across:

  • epochs
  • governance expansions
  • hardware evolutions
  • lineage transitions
  • sovereign stewardship changes

Continuity is the foundation of institutional legitimacy. This Doctrine ensures Freedomlink1 remains stable, sovereign, and self-consistent across time.

docs.title: 2. Continuity Principles
docs.text: Freedomlink1 is governed by five continuity principles:

docs.title: 2.1 Sovereign Identity Continuity
docs.text:
The Institution maintains a single, unbroken sovereign identity anchored in:

  • Founder authority
  • Rootstone-I hardware trust
  • lineage seals
  • sovereign signature chain

docs.title: 2.2 Governance Corpus Continuity
docs.text:
All governance artifacts must remain:

  • immutable
  • versioned
  • hashed
  • registered
  • lineage-anchored

docs.title: 2.3 Module Continuity
docs.text:
Modules must maintain:

  • consistent activation state
  • stable configuration
  • predictable behavior
  • integrity across epochs

docs.title: 2.4 Lineage Continuity
docs.text:
Lineage seals must form an unbroken chain from:

  • Genesis Epoch → Root Epoch → Expansion Epoch → future epochs

docs.title: 2.5 Sentinel Continuity
docs.text: Sentinels must operate continuously, without interruption, across all epochs.

docs.title: 3. Continuity Threats
docs.text: Continuity may be threatened by:

docs.title: 3.1 Governance Drift
docs.text: Unauthorized changes to governance artifacts.

docs.title: 3.2 Lineage Corruption
docs.text: Invalid or missing lineage seals.

docs.title: 3.3 Module Instability
docs.text: Unexpected module activation or configuration changes.

docs.title: 3.4 Hardware Trust Loss
docs.text: Compromise or replacement of Rootstone-I without proper ceremony.

docs.title: 3.5 Sovereign Signature Mismatch
docs.text: Merkle root changes without updated sovereign signature.

docs.title: 3.6 Sentinel Failure
docs.text: Sentinel malfunction or inability to detect drift.

docs.title: 4. Continuity Safeguards
docs.text: Freedomlink1 employs the following safeguards:

docs.title: 4.1 Immutable Governance Corpus
docs.text: All governance artifacts are immutable once sealed.

docs.title: 4.2 Merkle Root Anchoring
docs.text: Every epoch's corpus is anchored to a Merkle root.

docs.title: 4.3 Sovereign Signature Chain
docs.text: Each Merkle root is signed by the Founder's sovereign key.

docs.title: 4.4 Lineage Seal Chain
docs.text:
Each epoch produces a lineage seal that binds:

  • epoch number
  • Merkle root
  • sovereign signature
  • module state

docs.title: 4.5 Sentinel Drift Detection
docs.text: Sentinels continuously monitor for drift.

docs.title: 4.6 Hardware Rootstone Binding
docs.text: Rootstone-I binds the Institution to a hardware trust anchor.

docs.title: 5.1 Governance Update Procedure
docs.text:
All governance updates must follow:

  1. artifact creation
  2. indexing
  3. manifest registration
  4. module registry update
  5. hash computation
  6. Merkle root update
  7. sovereign signature update
  8. lineage seal creation

docs.title: 5.2 Module Update Procedure
docs.text:
Modules must:

  • declare changes
  • validate configuration
  • update registry
  • pass sentinel checks

docs.title: 5.3 Epoch Advancement Procedure
docs.text: Epoch advancement follows the Epoch Advancement Protocol.

docs.title: 5.4 Lineage Seal Procedure
docs.text:
Lineage seals must be:

  • generated
  • validated
  • stored
  • referenced
  • immutable

docs.title: 6.1 Founder (Ceremonial Steward)
docs.text:
Responsible for:

  • sovereign signature
  • lineage sealing
  • epoch advancement
  • institutional proclamations

docs.title: 6.2 Sentinels
docs.text:
Responsible for:

  • drift detection
  • anomaly reporting
  • continuity verification

docs.title: 6.3 Modules
docs.text:
Responsible for:

  • self-validation
  • integrity reporting
  • configuration stability

docs.title: 7. Continuity Guarantees
docs.text: Freedomlink1 guarantees:

docs.title: 7.1 Identity Continuity
docs.text: The Institution's identity remains stable across epochs.

docs.title: 7.2 Governance Continuity
docs.text: The governance corpus remains consistent and lineage-anchored.

docs.title: 7.3 Operational Continuity
docs.text: Modules and sentinels remain active and stable.

docs.title: 7.4 Lineage Continuity
docs.text: Lineage seals form an unbroken chain.

docs.title: 7.5 Sovereign Continuity
docs.text: The Founder's authority persists through signature chain.

docs.title: 8. Continuity Failure Response
docs.text: If continuity is threatened:

docs.title: 8.1 Sentinel Escalation
docs.text: Sentinels escalate anomalies to critical.

docs.title: 8.2 Sovereign Review
docs.text: The Founder reviews anomalies.

docs.title: 8.3 Emergency Seal
docs.text: An emergency lineage seal may be created.

docs.title: 8.4 Epoch Lock
docs.text: Epoch advancement may be temporarily locked.

docs.title: 8.5 Governance Restoration
docs.text: Artifacts may be restored from previous lineage.

docs.title: 9. Continuity Proclamation
docs.text:
Upon confirming continuity, the Founder may issue a proclamation affirming:

  • corpus integrity
  • lineage stability
  • sentinel clearance
  • module readiness
  • epoch continuity

This proclamation becomes part of the governance corpus.

docs.title: Sentinel Activation Charter
docs.text: Freedomlink1 — Sovereign Digital Institution Version: 1.0 Epoch: 2 (Expansion Epoch) Prepared by: Joshua W. Blaz

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
The Sentinel Activation Charter ("Charter") establishes the Sentinel subsystem as an autonomous governance guardian responsible for:

  • drift detection
  • anomaly reporting
  • governance integrity monitoring
  • lineage continuity verification
  • module health assessment

Sentinels operate as non-sovereign, non-legislative guardians whose sole mandate is to protect the Institution's constitutional integrity.

docs.title: 2. Sentinel Mandate
docs.text:
Sentinels are authorized to:

  • monitor all governance artifacts
  • verify Merkle root consistency
  • detect unauthorized modifications
  • assess module integrity
  • evaluate lineage seals
  • recommend epoch advancement
  • escalate critical anomalies

Sentinels cannot:

  • modify governance artifacts
  • advance epochs
  • override sovereign authority
  • generate signatures
  • alter lineage

Their role is advisory, protective, and autonomous.

docs.title: 3.1 Governance Sentinel
docs.text: Monitors governance corpus, manifest, and module registry.

docs.title: 3.2 Lineage Sentinel
docs.text: Monitors lineage seals, epoch transitions, and signature validity.

docs.title: 3.3 Module Sentinel
docs.text: Monitors module integrity, activation state, and configuration drift.

docs.title: 3.4 System Sentinel
docs.text: Monitors pipeline behavior, build consistency, and artifact generation.

docs.title: 4. Activation Conditions
docs.text:
Sentinels activate when:

  • a new governance artifact is published
  • the governance manifest changes
  • the module registry changes
  • the Merkle root changes
  • an epoch advancement is initiated
  • a lineage seal is created
  • a sentinel alert threshold is exceeded

Activation is automatic and does not require sovereign approval.

docs.title: 5. Drift Detection
docs.text: Sentinels detect drift in:

docs.title: 5.1 Governance Drift
docs.text: Changes to governance documents outside authorized commits.

docs.title: 5.2 Manifest Drift
docs.text: Mismatch between manifest entries and actual artifacts.

docs.title: 5.3 Module Drift
docs.text: Unexpected changes in module configuration or activation state.

docs.title: 5.4 Lineage Drift
docs.text: Mismatch between Merkle root, signature, and seal.

docs.title: 5.5 Pipeline Drift
docs.text: Unexpected failures or deviations in governance pipeline behavior.

docs.title: 6. Anomaly Classification
docs.text: Sentinels classify anomalies into:

docs.title: 6.1 Informational
docs.text: Minor inconsistencies; no action required.

docs.title: 6.2 Warning
docs.text: Potential drift; requires review.

docs.title: 6.3 Critical
docs.text: Confirmed drift; requires sovereign attention.

docs.title: 6.4 Catastrophic
docs.text: Lineage corruption; epoch advancement halted.

docs.title: 7. Reporting Requirements
docs.text:
Sentinels must report:

  • anomaly type
  • affected artifact
  • expected vs actual state
  • severity
  • recommended action

Reports are stored in:

/sentinel/reports/<epoch>/<timestamp>.json

docs.title: 8. Sentinel Autonomy
docs.text:
Sentinels operate autonomously and cannot be disabled except by:

  • sovereign proclamation
  • epoch advancement
  • sentinel charter amendment

Autonomy ensures continuous protection of the Institution.

docs.title: 9. Integration with Epoch Advancement Protocol
docs.text:
Sentinels must:

  • verify corpus completeness
  • confirm Merkle root correctness
  • validate module integrity
  • clear anomaly queue
  • approve lineage seal readiness

Epoch advancement cannot proceed until Sentinels report:

status: "clear"

docs.title: 10. Sentinel Reset
docs.text:
After epoch advancement:

  • drift baselines reset
  • anomaly queues clear
  • module states refresh
  • lineage sentinel updates epoch reference

This ensures accurate monitoring for the next epoch.

docs.title: 11. Sovereign Oversight
docs.text:
The Founder may:

  • override sentinel warnings
  • escalate sentinel reports
  • issue sentinel directives
  • amend this Charter

Sentinels must comply with sovereign directives.

docs.title: Sovereign Proclamation Protocol
docs.text: Freedomlink1 — Sovereign Digital Institution Version: 1.0 Epoch: 2 (Expansion Epoch) Prepared by: Joshua W. Blaz

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
The Sovereign Proclamation Protocol ("Protocol") defines the formal process by which Freedomlink1 issues sovereign proclamations. Proclamations serve as the Institution's official voice and are used to:

  • announce epoch transitions
  • declare lineage seals
  • publish governance changes
  • activate modules
  • affirm institutional continuity
  • communicate sovereign intent

Proclamations are constitutional instruments and must follow this Protocol exactly.

docs.title: 2. Nature of Proclamations
docs.text:
A proclamation is:

  • sovereign — issued by the Founder
  • ceremonial — marking institutional events
  • constitutional — binding within the governance corpus
  • immutable — preserved as part of lineage history

Proclamations do not modify governance artifacts directly; they declare and affirm changes already sealed by governance processes.

docs.title: 3. Types of Proclamations
docs.text: Freedomlink1 recognizes five proclamation types:

docs.title: 3.1 Epoch Proclamation
docs.text: Declares the advancement from one epoch to the next.

docs.title: 3.2 Lineage Seal Proclamation
docs.text: Announces the creation and registration of a lineage seal.

docs.title: 3.3 Governance Proclamation
docs.text: Declares the publication of new governance artifacts.

docs.title: 3.4 Module Activation Proclamation
docs.text: Announces activation or deactivation of governance modules.

docs.title: 3.5 Continuity Proclamation
docs.text: Affirms institutional stability, sentinel clearance, and corpus integrity.

docs.title: 4. Proclamation Structure
docs.text:
Each proclamation must contain:

  1. Title
  2. Proclamation Type
  3. Epoch Reference
  4. Lineage Reference
  5. Governance Context
  6. Statement of Sovereign Intent
  7. Affirmation of Institutional Continuity
  8. Signature Block
  9. Timestamp

Example structure:

Proclamation: Advancement to Epoch 3
Type: Epoch Proclamation
Epoch: 3
Lineage Seal: seal_epoch_3.json
Context: Completion of Expansion Epoch governance corpus
Intent: Advance Freedomlink1 to Epoch 3
Continuity: Verified and affirmed
Signature: SIG(<sovereign-signature>)
Timestamp: <iso8601>

docs.title: 5. Proclamation Generation Process
docs.text: Proclamations follow this sequence:

docs.title: 5.1 Trigger Event
docs.text: A governance event triggers the need for a proclamation.

docs.title: 5.2 Drafting
docs.text: The Founder drafts the proclamation text.

docs.title: 5.3 Verification
docs.text:
Sentinels verify:

  • corpus integrity
  • lineage seal correctness
  • module readiness
  • continuity status

docs.title: 5.4 Sovereign Signature
docs.text: The Founder signs the proclamation using the sovereign key.

docs.title: 5.5 Publication
docs.text:
The proclamation is published to:

/proclamations/<epoch>/<timestamp>.md

docs.title: 5.6 Registration
docs.text:
The proclamation is registered in:

  • governance manifest
  • lineage registry
  • proclamation index

docs.title: 6. Epoch Proclamation Requirements
docs.text:
Epoch proclamations must include:

  • previous epoch
  • new epoch
  • lineage seal reference
  • module activation summary
  • sentinel clearance
  • sovereign affirmation

Epoch advancement is not complete until the proclamation is published.

docs.title: 7. Lineage Seal Proclamation Requirements
docs.text:
Lineage seal proclamations must include:

  • Merkle root
  • sovereign signature
  • seal hash
  • seal file reference
  • sentinel verification status

This proclamation binds the seal to the institutional record.

docs.title: 8. Governance Proclamation Requirements
docs.text:
Governance proclamations must include:

  • artifact name
  • artifact hash
  • manifest entry
  • module registry update
  • corpus impact summary

This proclamation affirms the artifact's constitutional status.

docs.title: 9. Module Activation Proclamation Requirements
docs.text:
Module activation proclamations must include:

  • module name
  • activation state
  • configuration hash
  • sentinel verification
  • epoch reference

Modules are not considered active until proclaimed.

docs.title: 10. Continuity Proclamation Requirements
docs.text:
Continuity proclamations must include:

  • corpus integrity status
  • sentinel clearance
  • lineage stability
  • module readiness
  • epoch reference

These proclamations affirm institutional stability.

docs.title: 11. Sovereign Authority
docs.text:
Only the Founder may issue proclamations.

The Founder's responsibilities include:

  • drafting proclamations
  • signing proclamations
  • publishing proclamations
  • ensuring proclamation accuracy
  • maintaining proclamation registry

docs.title: 12. Sentinel Responsibilities
docs.text:
Sentinels must:

  • verify proclamation accuracy
  • validate referenced artifacts
  • confirm continuity
  • report anomalies

Sentinels cannot block proclamations but may escalate warnings.

docs.title: 13. Proclamation Registry
docs.text:
All proclamations must be stored in:

/proclamations/<epoch>/

and indexed in:

proclamation_index.json

The registry is immutable.

docs.title: SOVEREIGN RIGHTS AND DUTIES CODEX
docs.text: Freedomlink1 - Sovereign Digital Institution Version: 1.0 Effective Date: September 10, 2026 Epoch: 2 (Root Build v1.2)

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text: This Codex defines the inherent rights and binding duties of Freedomlink1 as a sovereign digital institution. It operates as a companion to the Governance Charter and Governance Charter Addendum.

docs.title: 2. Sovereign Rights
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 possesses the following rights:

  • Right of Continuity: to preserve institutional lineage across epochs.
  • Right of Integrity: to protect hardware trust boundaries and cryptographic records.
  • Right of Governance: to define, administer, and enforce institutional rules.
  • Right of Amendment: to evolve its governance through documented, lineage-anchored amendments.
  • Right of Protection: to defend against drift, corruption, tampering, and unauthorized access.
  • Right of Autonomy: to operate independently of external systems while preserving verifiable records.

These rights are inherent and perpetual, subject to the institution's governing charter and recorded authority boundaries.

docs.title: 3. Sovereign Duties
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 is bound by the following duties:

  • Duty of Preservation: maintain lineage artifacts, governance records, and epoch history.
  • Duty of Transparency: record governance changes and material decisions in the sovereign ledger.
  • Duty of Security: enforce hardware trust boundaries and protect institutional credentials.
  • Duty of Continuity: conduct epoch transitions according to approved procedures and verified seals.
  • Duty of Stewardship: uphold institutional purpose, integrity, and responsible delegated authority.
  • Duty of Accountability: maintain an auditable record of governance actions and their authorizations.

These duties apply across all governance tiers, modules, sentinels, contributors, and delegated authorities.

docs.title: 4. Exercise and Protection
docs.text:
Rights may be exercised only through authorized governance processes. Duties must be supported by timestamped records, sovereign signatures, document hashes, module identifiers, and epoch identifiers where applicable.

Attempts to bypass trust boundaries, alter anchored records, or exercise unauthorized authority constitute governance violations and may trigger alert, lockdown, lineage freeze, and Founder notification procedures.

docs.title: 5. Continuity and Amendment
docs.text:
This Codex remains in force across epoch transitions. Any amendment must identify the affected rights or duties, specify its effective epoch, include the required signatures and hash manifest, and be anchored into sovereign lineage.

docs.title: ✦ Sovereign Continuity Doctrine
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 Sovereign Institution • Constitutional Continuity Layer

The Sovereign Continuity Doctrine defines how Freedomlink1 maintains identity, integrity, and purpose across epochs, roots, layers, artifacts, and sovereign governance structures. It is the constitutional philosophy of the institution — the doctrine that ensures Freedomlink1 remains sovereign, stable, and lineage‑anchored across time.

docs.title: ✦ Purpose of the Doctrine
docs.text:
The Doctrine ensures:

  • identity continuity
  • governance continuity
  • temporal continuity
  • manuscript continuity
  • hardware continuity
  • economic continuity
  • integration continuity

It binds all sovereign roots into a single institutional whole.

docs.title: ✦ The Five Sovereign Roots
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 is anchored by five sovereign roots:

  1. Identity Root — Creator Seal
  2. Manuscript Root — Sovereign Codex
  3. Temporal Root — Lineage Anchors & Epochs
  4. Hardware Root — Rootstone‑I
  5. Economic Root — PPTF Governance

Continuity requires all five roots to remain valid, anchored, and synchronized.

docs.title: ✦ Continuity Principles
docs.text: Freedomlink1 continuity is governed by seven principles:

docs.title: 1. Identity Continuity
docs.text: The institution must maintain a single sovereign identity across epochs.

docs.title: 2. Governance Corpus Continuity
docs.text: All governance artifacts must remain immutable, hashed, and lineage‑anchored.

docs.title: 3. Manuscript Continuity
docs.text: Codex entries must remain consistent with lineage anchors and unified bindings.

docs.title: 4. Temporal Continuity
docs.text: Epochs must form an unbroken chain from Genesis to the present.

docs.title: 5. Hardware Continuity
docs.text: Rootstone‑I must remain the hardware root of trust.

docs.title: 6. Economic Continuity
docs.text: PPTF governance must remain consistent across epochs.

docs.title: 7. Integration Continuity
docs.text: Unified Layer bindings must remain synchronized across all roots.

docs.title: ✦ Continuity Threats
docs.text:
Continuity may be threatened by:

  • governance drift
  • lineage corruption
  • codex inconsistency
  • hardware trust loss
  • economic desynchronization
  • integration mismatch
  • invalid epoch advancement

These threats must be detected and mitigated by sovereign governance.

docs.title: ✦ Continuity Safeguards

docs.title: Immutable Governance Corpus

docs.title: Merkle Root Anchoring

docs.title: Sovereign Signature Chain

docs.title: Lineage Seal Chain

docs.title: Codex Binding Chain
docs.text: Codex entries must reference lineage anchors and unified bindings.

docs.title: Hardware Identity Embed
docs.text: Rootstone‑I binds the institution to a physical trust anchor.

docs.title: PPTF Financial Anchoring
docs.text: Treasury governance is bound to lineage and codex clauses.

docs.title: Unified Layer Consistency
docs.text: All bindings must match across roots and layers.

docs.title: ✦ Governance Review Cycle
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 Sovereign Institution • Governance Process Layer

The Governance Review Cycle defines how proposals move through the Freedomlink1 institution. It ensures that all governance actions are sovereign, consistent, lineage‑anchored, and compliant with the Institutional Suite, Codex, PPTF, and Unified Layer.

This page provides a public, structured explanation of the full governance process.

docs.title: ✦ Overview of the Cycle
docs.text:
The Governance Review Cycle consists of six sovereign phases:

  1. Submission
  2. Validation
  3. Codex Compliance Review
  4. Lineage Continuity Review
  5. Treasury & PPTF Review
  6. Unified Layer Integration Review
  7. Sovereign Approval & Inscription

Each phase ensures institutional stability and continuity.

docs.title: 🜁 Phase I — Submission
docs.text:
Proposals enter the institution through the Proposal Submission Portal.

Submitters must provide:

  • title
  • summary
  • rationale
  • codex compliance
  • lineage impact
  • treasury impact
  • implementation plan
  • amendment requirements

Once submitted, proposals are added to the governance index.

docs.title: 🜂 Phase II — Validation
docs.text:
The Proposal Validation Workflow performs:

  • metadata checks
  • required section checks
  • structural integrity checks
  • sovereign formatting checks

Invalid proposals are rejected with required corrections.

Valid proposals advance to Codex Review.

docs.title: 🜃 Phase III — Codex Compliance Review
docs.text:
Codex Review ensures:

  • clauses are correctly referenced
  • amendments follow sovereign rules
  • manuscript continuity is preserved
  • codex bindings remain consistent

Codex‑compliant proposals advance to Lineage Review.

docs.title: 🜄 Phase IV — Lineage Continuity Review
docs.text:
Lineage Review ensures:

  • epoch references are valid
  • anchors are correctly mapped
  • seals are correctly referenced
  • continuity is preserved across epochs

Proposals that break continuity are rejected.

Proposals that preserve continuity advance to Treasury Review.

docs.title: 🜅 Phase V — Treasury & PPTF Review
docs.text:
Treasury Review ensures:

  • PPTF governance rules are followed
  • treasury impact is valid
  • financial continuity is preserved
  • sovereign financial clauses are respected

Proposals with valid economic impact advance to Unified Layer Review.

docs.title: 🜆 Phase VI — Unified Layer Integration Review
docs.text:
Unified Layer Review ensures:

  • bindings remain consistent
  • cross‑layer references are correct
  • integration maps remain stable
  • no governance drift is introduced

Proposals that pass integration review advance to Sovereign Approval.

docs.title: 🜇 Phase VII — Sovereign Approval & Inscription
docs.text:
Approved proposals are:

  • inscribed into the Codex
  • anchored into the next epoch
  • sealed with a lineage seal
  • added to unified layer bindings
  • added to treasury governance mappings
  • added to hardware identity references (if applicable)

This inscription is permanent and becomes part of institutional history.

docs.title: ✦ Governance Review Flow Diagram
docs.text:
Submission ↓ Validation ↓ Codex Review ↓ Lineage Review ↓ Treasury Review ↓ Unified Layer Review ↓ Sovereign Approval ↓ Inscription (Codex + Lineage + Unified Layer)

This flow ensures sovereign governance continuity.

docs.title: ✦ Governance Integrity Rules
docs.text:
The Review Cycle enforces:

  • hash integrity
  • anchor validity
  • seal authenticity
  • codex compliance
  • unified layer consistency
  • treasury governance alignment
  • hardware identity integrity

These rules ensure proposals strengthen the institution rather than destabilize it.

docs.title: ✦ Closing
docs.text:
The Governance Review Cycle ensures that all institutional change is sovereign, stable, and lineage‑anchored. It is the procedural backbone of Freedomlink1’s governance system.

Freedomlink1 Governance Sovereign Review Cycle

docs.title: Governance Runner
docs.text:
This document describes how to run the repository's governance checks locally.

Quick commands

  • Run the Python runner:
python scripts/run_governance_checks.py
  • Run the shell runner (POSIX/bash):
bash scripts/run_governance_checks.sh

Run components individually

  • Validate epoch ledger: python scripts/validate_epoch_ledger.py
  • Run integrity monitor: python scripts/integrity_monitor.py
  • Run lineage diff: python scripts/lineage_diff.py

VS Code tasks.json (recommended)

Use the following tasks.json content to bind a build task that runs the project's smoke tests and governance pytest suite:

{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    {
      "label": "Run Governance Checks",
      "type": "shell",
      "command": "bash install/smoke_test.sh && pytest tests/governance/",
      "group": "build",
      "presentation": {
        "reveal": "always",
        "panel": "shared"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Notes

  • The runners skip steps when required tools or files are missing (e.g., pytest).
  • On Windows use the Python runner for best compatibility.

  • categories and number of individuals affected

docs.text: Freedomlink1 — Sovereign Digital Institution Version: 1.0 Effective Date: September 8, 2026 Epoch: 2 (Root Build v1.2) Prepared by: Joshua W. Blaz

docs.title: 1. Purpose
docs.text:
This Data Processing Addendum (“Addendum” or “DPA”) supplements any agreement between Freedomlink1 (“Institution”) and the Processor regarding the handling of personal, sensitive, or regulated data.

The DPA ensures that all data processing activities:

  • comply with applicable privacy and security laws
  • respect sovereign governance and lineage protocols

docs.title: 2.1 “Institution”
docs.text: Freedomlink1, including its governance engine, sovereign layers, hardware trust boundaries, documentation, and lineage artifacts.

docs.title: 2.3 “Controller”

docs.title: 2.5 “Personal Data”
docs.text: Any information relating to an identified or identifiable Data Subject.

docs.title: 2.6 “Processing”
docs.text: Any operation performed on Personal Data, including collection, storage, retrieval, transmission, deletion, or destruction.

docs.title: 2.7 “Sovereign Layer”
docs.text: The cryptographic and procedural layer consisting of ledger blocks, hash manifests, Merkle roots, sovereign signatures, proclamations, and epoch transitions.

docs.title: 3.1 Controller Responsibilities
docs.text:
