  • determines the purpose and means of processing
  • ensures lawful basis for processing
  • provides instructions to the Processor
  • maintains sovereign lineage records where applicable

docs.title: 3.2 Processor Responsibilities
docs.text:
The Processor shall:

  • process Personal Data only on documented instructions from the Institution
  • ensure confidentiality and security
  • comply with applicable privacy laws
  • maintain accurate records of processing activities
  • notify the Institution of any data incidents

docs.text:
Processor shall process Personal Data solely for:

  • operational support
  • technical services
  • analytics or reporting
  • governance module execution
  • hardware trust operations
  • documentation or institutional workflows

Processor shall not:

  • use Personal Data for its own purposes
  • sell or transfer Personal Data
  • modify sovereign lineage records
  • bypass hardware trust boundaries

docs.title: 5. Security Measures
docs.text:
Processor shall implement:

  • encryption in transit and at rest
  • access controls and authentication
  • secure storage and deletion protocols
  • hardware‑rooted trust mechanisms where applicable
  • audit logging and monitoring
  • incident detection and response procedures

Security measures must align with the Institution’s sovereign governance and hardware trust architecture.

docs.title: 6. Sub‑Processors
docs.text:

  • prior written approval from the Institution
  • ensuring sub‑processors comply with this DPA
  • maintaining a list of authorized sub‑processors

docs.title: 7. Data Subject Rights
docs.text:
Processor shall assist the Institution in responding to:

  • access requests
  • correction requests
  • deletion requests
  • restriction or objection requests
  • data portability requests

Processor shall not respond directly to Data Subjects unless authorized.

docs.title: 8. Data Breach Notification
docs.text:
Processor shall notify the Institution without undue delay upon becoming aware of:

  • unauthorized access
  • accidental loss
  • destruction
  • alteration
  • disclosure of Personal Data

Notification shall include:

  • nature of the breach
  • categories and number of Data Subjects affected
  • likely consequences
  • mitigation measures taken

docs.title: 9. Data Transfers
docs.text:
Processor shall not transfer Personal Data outside approved jurisdictions without:

  • lawful transfer mechanisms
  • encryption
  • sovereign governance approval
  • lineage recording where applicable

docs.title: 10. Return or Deletion of Data
docs.text:
Upon termination of services, Processor shall:

  • return all Personal Data to the Institution, or
  • securely delete all Personal Data

docs.title: 11. Sovereign Compliance

  • certain processing activities may be recorded in sovereign lineage

  • sovereign signatures may be required for compliance events
  • institutional proclamations may define future governance changes

docs.title: 12. Audit Rights
docs.text:
Institution may audit Processor’s compliance with this DPA, including:

  • security controls
  • data handling procedures
  • sub‑processor compliance
  • lineage‑related operations

Audits may be conducted by the Institution or an authorized third party.

docs.title: 13. Governing Law
docs.text: This DPA is governed by the laws of the State of Oklahoma, without regard to conflict‑of‑law principles.

docs.title: 14. Term and Termination
docs.text:
This DPA remains in effect as long as Processor processes Personal Data on behalf of the Institution.

Upon termination:

  • Processor shall cease processing
  • return or delete Personal Data
  • maintain confidentiality obligations

  3. A public proclamation
  4. Inclusion in the next epoch ledger

No Founder may be added informally or implicitly.

docs.text:
A Founder may be removed only through:

  • unanimous vote of all other Founders
  • issuance of a Removal Resolution
  • sovereign signature
  • publication in the next epoch ledger

Removal is a sovereign act and cannot occur silently.

docs.text:

  • changelogs

docs.title: 5.3 Duty of Ceremony
docs.text:

  • epoch sealing
  • proclamation issuance
  • signature block creation
  • lineage anchoring

docs.title: 6.1 Ownership
docs.text: All institutional artifacts, including hardware designs, governance modules, lineage files, and documentation, are owned collectively by the Founders.

docs.title: 6.2 Assignment
docs.text: Any Founder producing new institutional artifacts automatically assigns them to the Institution.

docs.title: 6.3 Protection
docs.text:
Founders must protect:

  • cryptographic secrets
  • hardware schematics
  • governance logic
  • institutional documents

from unauthorized disclosure.

docs.title: 7.1 Definition
docs.text:
A Founder Resolution is a formal decision recorded in:

  • the epoch ledger
  • the hash manifest
  • the sovereign signature block
  • the proclamation, if applicable

docs.title: 7.2 Requirements
docs.text:
A valid Resolution must include:

  • title
  • purpose
  • decision
  • signatures
  • timestamp
  • lineage references

docs.title: 7.3 Binding Nature
docs.text: Resolutions are binding until superseded by a later epoch.

docs.title: 8.1 Initiation
docs.text: An epoch transition may be initiated by any Founder.

docs.title: 8.2 Requirements
docs.text:

  • new ledger block
  • updated hash manifest
  • regenerated Merkle root
  • sovereign signature block
  • proclamation
  • public release

docs.title: 8.3 Finality
docs.text: Once sealed, an epoch becomes immutable.

docs.title: 9. Confidentiality
docs.text:

  • private keys
  • hardware fuse maps

  • unreleased governance modules

Confidentiality survives removal or resignation.

Disputes among Founders must be resolved through:

  • discussion
  • mediation

docs.title: 10.2 Sovereign Arbitration
docs.text:
If unresolved, disputes are arbitrated through:

  • a sovereign signature block
  • a formal proclamation
  • inclusion in the next epoch ledger

docs.title: 11.1 Method
docs.text:
This Agreement may be amended only through:

  • unanimous Founder approval

  • sovereign signature
  • publication in the next epoch ledger

docs.title: 11.2 Prohibition

docs.title: Ceremony Checklist Template
docs.text:
Purpose: Standard checklist to record procedures, artifacts, and verification for governance ceremonies (activation, promotion, retirement, succession, epoch advancement).

Audience: Steward, Custodians, Sentinel operators, Recorders.

Checklist 1. Preparation - Confirm ceremony type and justification - Notify custodians and sentinels (Slack + Email) - Schedule time and designate recorder - Ensure required artifacts exist (merkle_root.txt, hash_manifest.json, relevant artifacts)

  1. Pre-Verification
  2. Run: python3 scripts/validate_epoch_ledger.py (if epoch-related)
  3. Run: python3 scripts/integrity_monitor.py
  4. Run: python3 scripts/lineage_diff.py to detect drift

  5. Confirm signatures and hashes are present and valid

  6. Ceremony Execution

  7. Read invocation and present the subject (e.g., Sentinel ID, Module ID, Steward identity)
  8. Perform required script actions:
    • Activation/Promotion/Retirement: update registry via scripts/update_sentinel_registry.py or scripts/retire_module.py
    • Succession: python3 scripts/update_steward_registry.py "Name" "<pubkey>" "<fingerprint>"
    • Epoch advancement: python3 scripts/advance_epoch.py

  9. Steward signs artifacts (manual step): merkle_root.txt, hash_manifest.json, epoch_ledger.json

  10. Post-Ceremony (Recorder)

  11. Update lineage/* registries as required
  12. Run: python3 scripts/build_merkle_tree.py hash_manifest.json merkle_root.txt
  13. Update artifacts/omni_proof_master.json with new signature (manual)
  14. Run: python3 scripts/update_logbook.py "<Ceremony> Completed: details..."

  15. Run integrity monitor once more: python3 scripts/integrity_monitor.py

  16. Artifacts to attach

  17. Ceremony minutes (text/markdown)
  18. Signed artifacts (paths)
  19. Commit/PR URL and run logs

  20. Updated registries and snapshots (lineage/last_integrity_snapshot.json)

  21. Approvals

  22. Steward signature (required)
  23. Custodian confirmations (list names)

  24. Sentinel validation (if automated)

  25. Publication

  26. Commit changes and push to main via PR with the ceremony checklist attached
  27. Publish governance_logbook entry and link to PR

Example commands

python3 scripts/lineage_diff.py
python3 scripts/update_logbook.py "Sentinel GS-03 Activated by Steward"
git add lineage/* artifacts/* && git commit -m "Ceremony: Activate GS-03" && git push

Notes - Preserve manual signature steps as human actions — they must remain auditable. - Keep this checklist inside the PR so auditors can verify ceremony compliance.

docs.title: ✦ Unified Layer Explorer
docs.text:
Freedomlink1 Sovereign Institution • Integration Layer

The Unified Layer is the institutional wiring of Freedomlink1 — the binding system that connects governance artifacts, lineage anchors, codex entries, hardware identity, and PPTF structures into a single sovereign whole.

This explorer provides a structured interface for viewing Unified Layer bindings, integration maps, sovereign wiring, and cross‑layer relationships.

docs.title: ✦ Unified Layer Overview
docs.text:
The Unified Layer integrates five sovereign roots:

  • Institutional Suite — legal governance
  • Sovereign Codex — manuscript governance
  • Lineage Anchors — temporal governance
  • Rootstone‑I — hardware governance
  • PPTF — economic governance

Together, these form the institutional backbone of Freedomlink1.

docs.title: 🜁 Unified Bindings File
docs.text:
Path: unified/pptf.bindings.json

This file contains the machine‑readable bindings for:

  • Institutional Suite artifacts
  • Codex entries
  • Lineage anchors
  • PPTF governance objects
  • Rootstone‑I identity references

It is the canonical representation of institutional integration.

docs.title: 🜂 Institutional Suite Bindings
docs.text:
The Institutional Suite is bound into the Unified Layer through:

  • Trust Charter
  • Grantor Declaration
  • Agency Charter
  • Treasury Governance
  • PPTF Integration
  • Governance Proclamations

Each artifact is mapped to:

  • its SHA‑256 hash
  • its Codex entry
  • its lineage anchor
  • its sovereign clause references
  • its epoch inscription

These bindings ensure legal governance is cryptographically anchored.

docs.title: 🜃 Codex Bindings
docs.text:
Codex entries are integrated through:

  • codex.bindings.json
  • manuscript → machine mappings
  • clause → anchor references
  • inscription → epoch references

This ensures manuscript governance is synchronized with temporal and legal layers.

docs.title: 🜄 Lineage Bindings
docs.text:
Lineage anchors and seals are integrated through:

  • epoch_5_institutional_anchor.json
  • epoch_5_institutional_seal.json
  • lineage.version

These bindings ensure temporal continuity is preserved across epochs.

docs.title: 🜅 Rootstone‑I Bindings
docs.text:
Rootstone‑I is integrated through:

  • rootstone-identity.json
  • hardware → codex references
  • hardware → lineage references
  • hardware → unified flags

This ensures hardware sovereignty participates in institutional continuity.

docs.title: 🜆 PPTF Bindings
docs.text:
PPTF governance objects are integrated through:

  • pptf.bindings.json
  • treasury governance mappings
  • economic continuity rules
  • sovereign financial clauses

This ensures economic governance is bound to legal, temporal, and manuscript layers.

docs.title: ✦ Integration Map
docs.text:
The Unified Layer forms a five‑way integration map:

Institutional Suite ↕ Sovereign Codex ↕ Lineage Anchors ↕ Rootstone‑I ↕ PPTF Governance

Each layer references the others through:

  • hashes
  • anchors
  • seals
  • clauses
  • manifests
  • bindings

This creates a sovereign, tamper‑resistant institutional architecture.

docs.title: ✦ Unified Integrity Rules
docs.text:
The Unified Layer enforces:

  • Hash Consistency
  • Anchor Validity
  • Seal Verification
  • Codex Compliance
  • Hardware Identity Integrity
  • Treasury Governance Consistency

These rules ensure the institution remains sovereign and stable.

docs.title: ✦ Closing
docs.text:
